articles.title: Mac 进入触屏时代：苹果铺路软件生态，11 月开启在线研讨
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 29 日消息，科技媒体 9to5Mac 今天（10 月 29 日）发布博文，苹果官方开发者网站已上线“为 Mac 触控做好准备”（Get ready for Touch on Mac）专题页面，为首批触屏 Mac 的软件生态做准备。IT之家附上相关视频如下：Mac 触控设计为 Mac 应用带来触控体验将实时活动引入 Mac苹果目前上线了三段视频，分别聚焦“Mac 触控设计”、“为 Mac 应用带来触控体验”以及“将实时活动引入 Mac”。这些内容旨在指导开发者重新思考光标、手势、界面层级与多任务场景，让应用在键盘、触控板和触屏之间都能保持自然、高效的体验。苹果公司还计划开放两场“与苹果见面”（Meet with Apple）在线小组实验室。开发者可与苹果工程师和设计师实时交流，就触控应用的创建、优化、交互设计等问题获得建议。两场活动分别安排在太平洋时间 11 月 18 日上午 9 点至 10 点（北京时间 11 月 19 日 1 点到 2 点），以及 11 月 19 日下午 6 点至 7 点（北京时间 11 月 20 日上午 10 点到 11 点），报名已经开启。

articles.content: IT之家 10 月 29 日消息，苹果公司今天（10 月 29 日）更新其“Apple 设计资源”门户网站，为首款配备 PROLED XDR 显示屏、支持触控的全新 MacBook Pro 提供官方设计素材。UI / UX 设计师、开发者及内容创作者无需等待第三方模板，即可在官方素材基础上制作适配新机的界面演示、宣传图和应用展示内容。IT之家援引博文介绍，此次新增的可下载 .dmg 文件包含新款 MacBook Pro 的透明 PNG 图像，覆盖不同配色与尺寸；同时提供 PSD 文件，已精确遮罩显示屏区域。设计师可以直接将自家的界面、网页布局或应用画面置入屏幕区域，快速生成高保真的产品效果图。苹果的设计资源门户长期为开发者与设计师提供覆盖苹果平台、产品和技术的设计指南，以及 Figma、Sketch、Keynote、Photoshop、PDF、PNG、SVG 等多格式素材；此外还包括字体、SF Symbols、图标编辑器、视差预览器。参考点此前往苹果官网下载其首款触控 MacBook Pro 设计素材

articles.title: 苹果首款触控 MacBook Pro 低音下潜增强 50%，首次调教合盖场景音频
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 29 日消息，苹果公司今天（10 月 29 日）发布新闻稿，宣布在其搭载 PROLED XDR 显示屏的首款触控 MacBook Pro 上，并重点升级其音频系统。官方表示这款 MacBook Pro 采用 6 扬声器音频系统，采用全新低音单元设计，低音下潜增强 50%，声音更深沉、更丰富。而全新高音单元可塑造声音扩散方式，让音质格外清晰、通透。这款 MacBook Pro 支持杜比全景声空间音频，用户在听音乐和看电影时营造沉浸式空间声场。苹果还引入录音棚级麦克风，提升通话、录音和语音命令的清晰度与干净度。IT之家援引博文介绍，MacBook Pro 还首次针对合上盖子时的使用场景进行了音频调教，在连接外接显示器时可呈现卓越音质，让用户无论以何种方式工作，都能享受高品质音频体验。

articles.content: IT之家 10 月 29 日消息，苹果公司今天（10 月 29 日）发布配备 PROLED XDR 显示屏的首款触控 MacBook Pro 外，还更新推出了 70W 充电器、全球旅行转换器套件等多款配件产品。一、70W 电源适配器（点此前往苹果官网选购）该产品售价为 449 元，IT之家附上官方介绍如下：无论是在家中、办公室还是旅行途中，这款 70W 电源适配器都能让你快速而高效地充电。它兼容多款 USB-C 设备和充电线。Apple 建议将它用于 14 英寸 MacBook Pro 或者 13 英寸或 15 英寸 MacBook Air，并搭配 USB-C 转 MagSafe 3 连接线或 USB-C 充电线。用这款电源适配器给 MacBook Air 充电，能充分发挥快充优势，约 30 分钟最多可充至 50% 电量。充电线需单独购买。这款 70W 电源适配器兼容配备交流电源接口 2 的配件，包括电源适配器延长线 (交流电源接口 2) 和全球旅行转换器套件。二、全球旅行转换器套件（点此前往苹果官网选购）该产品售价为 299 元，官方介绍如下：Apple 电源适配器经过精心设计，让你在众多国家和地区能够安全地为 Apple 设备充电。搭配这款全球旅行转换器套件，在出国旅行时，你可以轻松更换兼容的 Apple 电源适配器的交流电源插头，以适配当地的电源插座。套件内含五种可互换的交流电源插头：A 型插头：北美、日本C 型插头：欧洲大陆、巴西D 型插头：印度G 型插头：英国、阿联酋、沙特阿拉伯、新加坡I 型插头：澳大利亚、新西兰三、140W 充电器（点此前往苹果官网选购）该产品售价为 729 元，官方介绍如下：无论是在家中、办公室还是旅行途中，这款 140W 电源适配器都能让你快速而高效地充电。它兼容多款 USB-C 设备和充电线。Apple 建议将它用于 16 英寸 MacBook Pro，并搭配 USB-C 转 MagSafe 3 连接线或 USB-C 充电线来快速充电，约 30 分钟最多可充至 50% 电量。充电线需单独购买。这款 140W 电源适配器兼容配备交流电源接口 2 的配件，包括电源适配器延长线 (交流电源接口 2) 和全球旅行转换器套件。四、电源适配器延长线 (交流电源接口 2)（点此前往苹果官网选购）该产品售价为 145 元，官方介绍如下：这款 1.8 米的电源适配器延长线是交流电延长线缆，可延长你的 Apple 电源适配器的线缆长度。交流电源接口 2 兼容：70W 电源适配器140W 电源适配器苹果公司在官方日志中表示，为了符合新法规，其更新后的电源适配器、延长线和插头均采用椭圆形设计，而苹果之前的“交流电源接口 1”接口采用的是凹槽设计。“交流电源接口 1”接口五、Beats USB-C 转 USB-C 编织连接线 (1.5 米 / 5 英尺) – 超能粉（点此前往苹果官网选购）该产品售价为 145 元，官方介绍如下：全新编织连接线经过强化加固，助你提升充电体验，告别线缆缠绕、打结和磨损的困扰。Beats 1.5 米 (5 英尺) USB‑C 转 USB‑C 充电线采用防缠结的编织设计，极其耐用和便捷。Beats 连接线在设计和制造过程中历经了数千小时的测试，并且经过加固以防磨损。这款编织连接线兼容各种配备 USB-C 接口的 Apple 和安卓设备，可用于充电、同步、聆听音频、连接 CarPlay 车载和传输数据。借助这款连接线，你可以为兼容 USB-C 的 Beats 耳机或扬声器充电，同时欣赏音频或在线聆听无损音频。它支持以最高达 60 瓦的功率快速充电，并能以 USB 2.0 的速率传输数据。要快速高效地充电，可将这款 USB-C 连接线与 USB-C 电源适配器搭配使用，通过电源插座便捷地为兼容的 iPhone 或其他设备充电。USB-C 电源适配器需另购。六、Beats USB-A 转 USB-C 编织连接线 (1.5 米 / 5 英尺) – 超能粉（点此前往苹果官网选购）该产品售价为 145 元，官方介绍如下：全新编织连接线经过强化加固，助你提升充电体验，告别线缆缠绕、打结和磨损的困扰。Beats 1.5 米 USB-A 转 USB-C 充电线采用防缠结的编织设计，格外耐用和便捷。Beats 连接线在设计和制造过程中历经了数千小时的测试，并且经过加固以防磨损。这款编织连接线可用于充电、同步、连接 CarPlay 车载和传输数据，在指定 iPhone 和 iPad 上支持以最高达 15 瓦的功率快速充电，并以 USB 2.0 速率传输数据。电源适配器需另购。

articles.title: 最高 128GB 统一内存：苹果首款触控 MacBook Pro 可本地运行数千亿参数 AI 模型
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 29 日消息，苹果公司今天（10 月 29 日）发布配备 PROLED XDR 显示屏的首款触控 MacBook Pro，其核心卖点之一是配备最高 128GB 统一内存，M5 Max 芯片版可本地运行数千亿参数的大语言模型。IT之家附上官方公告内容如下：依托 M5 Max，专业人士可在设备端直接运行具有数千亿参数的大语言模型，并为精细视觉特效、3D 动画项目、电影配乐和 8K 视频后期制作等高强度工作流加速。苹果表示，M5 Pro 与 M5 Max 的每个 GPU 核心均内置神经网络加速器，可加速本地 AI 推理，并支持运行编程智能体、处理图形密集型 AI 任务等场景。苹果称依托 MacBook Pro 的强大 AI 性能，创意技术人员、3D 艺术家和动效设计师可在 LM Studio 等 app 中本地运行大语言模型，并在 TouchDesigner 等 app 中利用 AI 加速创意工作流，享受卓越性能和设备端处理带来的隐私保护。对需要处理敏感资料的用户而言，本地运行的价值在于隐私与可控性：文档、代码、图像和对话上下文不必发送到第三方服务器，本地模型可以完成代码分析、内容生成、资料整理等任务。配备 PROLED XDR 显示屏的首款触控 MacBook Pro 将于 10 月 30 日晚 9 点开启预购，11 月 6 日正式发售；中国大陆 14 英寸机型起售价为 22,999 元，16 英寸机型起售价为 27,999 元。

articles.title: 苹果触屏 MacBook Pro 应用适配情况：Lightroom、达芬奇、C4D、Office 等今年晚些时候支持

articles.title: 时隔 10 年发光 Logo 回归：苹果首款触控屏 MacBook Pro“苹果标”又会亮了
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 29 日消息，苹果在今天的特别活动中正式推出了首款触控屏 MacBook Pro（配备 PROLED XDR 显示屏的 MacBook Pro），值得一提的是，该机重新为 A 面带回了发光苹果 Logo。回顾历史，苹果从 1999 年 PowerBook G3 系列开始为笔记本 A 面引入发光苹果 Logo，相应 Logo 并没有配备任何独立的 LED 光源，而是直接“借用”了屏幕自身的背光。具体而言，苹果在 CNC 切割铝合金 A 面时，会在正中央镂空切出苹果 Logo 的形状，并在该孔位嵌入一块高透光率、表面经过磨砂雾面处理的白色聚碳酸酯（塑料）导光板。在屏幕面板内部的反光遮罩层上，苹果也精确对应 Logo 的位置预留了一个没有反光材料的透光区域。当用户打开电脑、屏幕背光亮起时，背光源产生的光线主要向前发散点亮屏幕。但由于遮罩层中心有预留孔洞，一部分光线会向后“漏”出。这部分光线正好打在 A 面的聚碳酸酯板上，经过磨砂材质的均匀漫反射，最终在机身外部呈现出柔和、无光斑的白色发光 Logo。2016 年之后，由于 MacBook 系列开始追求进一步轻薄化，在超薄铝合金上开大孔会降低结构强度，且因逆向漏光问题会影响专业级视网膜屏幕的色彩准确度。因此，苹果在 2015 年发布的 12 英寸 MacBook 上率先改用镜面金属（不锈钢）Logo，随后于 2016 年改版的 MacBook Pro（Touch Bar 款）上全面取消了发光设计，改用反光金属材质。如今，苹果正式发布了首款触控屏 MacBook Pro，经典的发光苹果 Logo 时隔 10 年宣告回归。由于新一代产品采用串联式 OLED 显示屏，相应面板本身是每个像素独立自发光，不再使用传统 LCD 背光方案，因此苹果为笔记本 A 面新版的发光 Logo 配备了独立的光源结构，在技术原理上与此前的发光 Logo 存在一定差异。IT之家注意到，在今天发布会结束后，苹果现 CEO 特努斯也把 X 平台头像换成了其使用 MacBook Pro 的照片，可以看到相应笔记本 Logo 标识度相当显眼。

articles.title: 5499 元起，苹果 iPad mini（A20 Pro）开启预购（国补后低至 4999 元起）
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 29 日闪讯速报，苹果旗下 iPad mini（A20 Pro）现已开启预购，该机也就是俗称的“iPad mini 8”。其搭载 8.5 英寸 OLED 屏幕，比上一代薄了 14%，采用 A20 Pro 芯片，11 月 6 日正式发售，定价 5,499 元起（国补后低至 4999 元起）。京东 Apple / 苹果 iPad mini (A20 Pro) 平板电脑 5499 元起直达链接IT之家附系列产品各版本定价如下：128GB：Wi-Fi 版 5,499 元，Wi-Fi+ 蜂窝版 6,799 元256GB：Wi-Fi 版 6,299 元，Wi-Fi+ 蜂窝版 7,599 元512GB：Wi-Fi 版本 7,999 元，Wi-Fi+ 蜂窝版 9,299 元据介绍，iPad mini（A20 Pro）提供午夜色、星光色两种配色。其机身相比上一代薄了 14%，轻了 13%。该机配备超视网膜 XDR 显示屏，采用 OLED 技术，峰值亮度可达 1,200 nits，支持 P3 广色域，对比度可达 2000000:1，不支持 ProMotion，256GB 和 512GB 机型可选配纳米纹理玻璃。性能方面，iPad mini（A20 Pro）搭载 A20 Pro 芯片，其封装方式借鉴了 M 系列芯片。每个图形处理器核心均内置全新神经网络加速器，为 Apple 智能和各种 AI 任务加速。该平板 CPU 性能相比 iPad mini 7 提速至 1.6 倍，图形处理器性能提升至 2.7 倍。需要注意的是，128GB 版和 256GB 版 iPad mini（A20 Pro）采用的 A20 Pro 芯片为 5 核 CPU（2 * 超级核心、3 * 能效核心）、7 核 GPU，以及 16 核 NPU；512GB 机型为 6 核 CPU（2 * 超级核心、4 * 能效核心）、7 核 GPU，以及双 16 核 NPU。同时，该平板配备 1,200 万像素后置摄像头，拥有自适应原彩闪光灯，最高支持 4K 60FPS 视频拍摄。前摄为 1,200 万像素 Center Stage，支持 1080P 60FPS 视频拍摄。该平板还拥有定制高音单元和低音单元，以及前后双麦克风，带来更加细腻的个人化音频感受。iPad mini（A20 Pro）采用 Apple N1 无线网络芯片，支持高速无线局域网、蓝牙 6 和 Thread 家庭网络技术。蜂窝网络机型采用 Apple C2 基带，支持 eSIM 。兼容 Apple Pencil Pro、Apple Pencil (USB‑C)，支持悬停功能。该平板具备 IP67 级防尘防水，在最深 1 米的水下停留时间最长可达 30 分钟。京东 11.11 无门槛红包 面额至高 26888 元，每天抽 3 次：点此抽红包。淘宝 11.11 无门槛红包 面额至高 26888 元，每天抽 1 次：点此抽红包。

articles.content: IT之家 10 月 29 日消息，苹果在今天的特别活动中正式推出了首款触控屏 MacBook Pro（配备 PROLED XDR 显示屏的 MacBook Pro），系列产品 10 月 30 日 9 点接受预购，11 月 6 日发售，22,999 元起，IT之家随附官方商店地址（点此访问）。系列笔记本可选 14.2/16.3 英寸版本，前者尺寸为 21.63 厘米 x31.08 厘米 x1.50 厘米，重 1.38 千克；后者尺寸为 24.42 厘米 x35.55 厘米 x1.60 厘米，重 1.82 千克。笔记本 C 面仍配备指纹识别触控 ID，笔记本可选 M5 Pro/M5 Max 芯片（至高可选 M5 Max：18 核中央处理器、16 核神经网络引擎版本），提供至高 24 小时续航。IT之家获悉，相应屏幕为双层串联 OLED ProMotion 1Hz-120Hz 自适应刷新率触控屏（官方称之为“PROLED XDR 显示屏”），提供 1000 尼特持续全屏亮度、2000 尼特 HDR 和 SDR 峰值亮度，覆盖 P3 + Adobe RGB 广色域。还提供了 iPhone 用户熟悉的“灵动岛”（1200 万像素 Center Stage 摄像头）。苹果表示，在设计层面，官方将触控传感器直接嵌入显示面板，而非加在表层，这让延迟大大降低，用起来就像是直接在触控内容本身。无论是滚动浏览，还是双指开合缩放，各种日常操作自然又灵敏。用户可以直接在屏上使用多点触控手势，滚动、双指开合、旋转、绘制等，各种妙用随手施展。官方强调，该机搭载重新设计的六扬声器系统，音质更纯净，低音下潜增强 50%，更加深沉浑厚。还配备录音棚级三麦克风阵列，收音效果清晰又响亮。笔记本配备三个雷雳 5 端口、一个 HDMI 端口、一个 MagSafe 3 端口、一个 SDXC 卡插槽、一个耳机插孔，支持高速 Wi-Fi 和蓝牙 6。

articles.title: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5 基准上线，DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 为 FrontierCode 2.0 开源模型最高成绩
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 29 日消息，Artificial Analysis 昨日发布了 Intelligence Index v5，这是该机构自 2026 年 1 月 v4 上线以来幅度最大的一次基准重构。最直接的变化是，60% 的评测权重首次建立在私有测试集或隐藏答案之上，用于压缩公开题库被模型训练数据“污染”的空间，减少了各厂商为了跑分而跑分的“注水”测试项目。该指数仍由九项评测构成，包括知识工作、编码、科学、通用能力各占 25%。其中编码 25% 的权重里，Cognition 于同日发布的 FrontierCode 2.0 独占 15%，Terminal-Bench 4.0 占 10%。其中最值得关注的 FrontierCode 2.0 完全换了一套评分逻辑。132 项任务全部来自真实开源仓库，模型提交的代码改动不再只由单元测试是否通过来判定，而是由该仓库的维护者按“是否愿意合并这个 PR”来打分，任何一项阻塞性检查失败即记零分。Cognition 在 6 月推出 FrontierCode 初版时就强调，传统基准只检查代码能否跑通，而合并决策还涉及改动范围是否克制、风格是否与代码库一致、回归风险是否可控等测试无法完全覆盖的维度。v5 将这一基准升级到 2.0 并纳入主指数，等于把“可合并性”而非“可运行性”推到了编码能力评价的中心。在这一口径下，DeepSeek V4.1-Flash 1017（max）在 FrontierCode 2.0 上录得 28%，是所有已发布权重模型中得分最高的一个。Kimi K3.1 Pro 以 25.5% 紧随其后，但其完整权重按月之暗面官方博客的表述，要到 11 月 4 日前才发布，AA 在 v5 报告中将其标注为“weights not yet released”。谷歌 Gemini 4 Argon（high）为 25.7%，GPT-6 Luna 为 25.2%，均低于 DeepSeek V4.1 Flash。需要说明的是，这一成绩位于 FrontierCode 2.0 单项之内；在 Intelligence Index v5 的综合得分上，DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 与 GLM-5.3 同为 32 分，仍落后榜首 Claude Opus 5.5（58 分）26 分，且低于 Claude Haiku 5.5 的 36 分。Artificial Analysis 指出，v5 真正加剧的是开源与闭源前沿之间的整体距离。v4.3 时，最强开源模型与榜首的差距是 3 分；v5 把大部分公开题换成私有题、并大幅加重智能体实战任务的比重之后，这一差距扩大到 12 分。Kimi K3.1 Pro 以 46 分成为名义上最强的开源权重模型，但它尚未发布权重；已发布权重的模型中，32 分是当前的天花板。差距在 HLE-Diamond 和 Terminal-Bench-Science 两项上最为刺眼：Kimi K3.1 Pro 分别为 37% 和 34%，而 Claude Opus 5.5 在 HLE-Diamond 上为 68%，GPT-6 Astra 在 Terminal-Bench-Science 上为 63%。v5 并没有让开源模型“一夜变差”，它改变的是测量的东西 —— 当题目不再公开、评分不再只看通过率，那些依靠公开题库优化出来的分数被系统性地挤掉了水分。另一个被 v5 放大的变量是“努力值”（思考等级）的成本优势。Claude Opus 5.5 从低努力档到 max 档跨越 23 分，单任务成本从 0.98 美元升至 10.04 美元，相差约 10 倍。Claude Sonnet 5.5 在不同努力档之间的分差从 v4.3 的 20 分扩大到 29 分，GPT-6.1 Sol 的跨度翻倍至 20 分。这意味着同一模型在“省钱模式”和“全力模式”下的表现差距，已经大到不像一个模型。在得分最高的十款模型中，GPT-6.1 Terra 的每任务成本最低，为 0.96 美元，Claude Fable 5.1 最高，为 13.04 美元，相差超过 13 倍。与 v5 同步推出的 Progress Index v1 则处理另一个问题：当基准本身每隔几个月就换一次，不同年代的模型如何放在同一把尺子上比较。Progress Index 将 2022 年 11 月以来发布的主要语言模型映射到一个连续的能力尺度上，其设计参考了 Epoch AI 的 Epoch Capabilities Index 的方法。Intelligence Index 继续作为衡量“当下前沿”的主指标，Progress Index 则用于观察“能力随时间如何演进”，两者回答的是不同问题。实际上，v5 的九项评测中没有任何一个模型

articles.title: 苹果线上商城下线维护，预估迎接其首款触控 MacBook Pro
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 29 日消息，太平洋时间 10 月 28 日上午 10 点（北京时间 10 月 29 日凌晨 1 点）在洛杉矶举行的“Pro and Tell”体验活动开始前几分钟，苹果官网在线商店已临时下线维护，这一动作通常被视为新品即将上架的信号。IT之家访问苹果中国官网在线商店，已经显示为“稍等一下，我们正在更新 Apple Store，请稍后再来。”根据目前曝光的信息和线索，苹果公司计划推出其首款触控屏 MacBook Pro。新款 MacBook Pro 有望首次配备支持触控的 OLED 显示屏，取消传统刘海屏并改用“灵动岛”设计；机身将更轻、更薄，铰链与散热系统也会重新设计。产品预计搭载 M5 Pro 与 M5 Max 芯片，而新版 macOS Golden Gate 则可能针对触控输入进行优化。价格方面，报道援引的消息称，14 英寸机型在美国起售价约为 2,899 美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 19,368 元人民币），16 英寸机型约为 3,399 美元（现汇率约合 22,709 元人民币）。若信息属实，这将是苹果 Mac 产品线近年来最重要的一次形态变化：触屏 MacBook 长期以来被外界视为苹果“不会做”的产品，此次若正式亮相，意味着苹果正在重新评估键盘、触控板与触屏在专业笔记本上的关系。

articles.title: 具身智能军备竞赛，胜负手在工程生态
articles.content: 开源工程底座 FluxVLA Engine 技术报告全解读。    作者丨邓哲敏    编辑丨齐铖湧                                                                                                       一个模型在论文中取得好成绩，距离它真正驱动机器人完成任务，还有多远？模型能否接入现有的数据与训练流程，推理速度能否跟上机器人的控制节奏，生成的动作能否连续、稳定地执行，实验结果又能否在不同机器人上得到验证——这些问题，未必能靠再提升几个百分点的模型成功率来解决。过去半年，AI科技评论（雷峰网）在与业内人士交流时发现，一些反复出现的工程问题正在消耗大量研发资源：不同模型的数据格式难以统一，训练和评测流程各自为政，仿真中的结果到了真机上未必成立；好不容易跑通一套流程，换个模型、换份数据或换台机器人，又可能需要重新适配。模型在不断迭代，工程积累却未必能随之沉淀。这让雷峰网想起深度学习的发展历程。2017 年，PyTorch 正式开源，此后，框架、工具链与开发者社区不断完善，研究者得以在更成熟的基础设施上开展实验，而不必每次从底层重新搭建环境。今天的具身智能虽然面临不同的技术挑战，但同样需要解决一个问题：如何让已有的研发成果更容易复用，让不同技术路线能够在统一的工程框架下协作。逐际动力开源的 FluxVLA Engine，试图从工程层面回应这一问题。它并非又一个争夺模型性能排名的 VLA 模型，而是一套面向具身智能研发的工程底座，贯通数据、训练、评测、推理与真机部署。10 月 22 日，FluxVLA Engine 完成重要更新。我们拆解了它的最新技术报告，并重点关注四个问题：不同架构的模型能否接入同一套研发体系？模型从仿真走向真机，需要跨过哪些工程障碍？真实交互经验如何低成本地回流到模型优化中？当同一套流程覆盖更多模型与机器人时，它究竟展示出了怎样的能力？01新模型请先登记一套工程底座是否真正有用，首先要看它能否接纳不同的模型。对具身智能来说，模型是迭代最快的。今天使用一种 VLA 架构，明天可能尝试另一种动作生成方式；同一团队也可能同时研究多个策略模型。如果每换一次模型，就要重新整理数据、编写评测代码、改造部署接口，那么此前积累的工程经验很难持续发挥价值。模型可以不断更换，但围绕数据、评测和部署建立起来的工程能力，不应该每次都从头再来。FluxVLA Engine 的做法，是通过统一配置与组件注册机制，把不同模型接入研发流程时需要处理的差异，尽可能收敛到明确的接口中。可以理解为一份统一的实验清单，加上一套可供调用的组件目录。配置文件负责声明一次实验需要使用什么模型、如何处理数据、怎样开展评测，以及通过什么接口进行部署。注册机制则将视觉骨干、动作头、训练运行器和机器人相关操作组件等分别组织起来。开发者可以按需组合已经适配的组件，而不必为每一种模型重新搭建整套工程流程。这并不意味着任何模型都能在不做适配的情况下直接运行。不同架构仍然可能需要各自的适配器、动作空间转换和归一化处理。真正的价值在于：把不可避免的差异放到可管理的组件层，让已经打通的公共流程能够继续复用。从技术报告来看，FluxVLA 已经将多种架构差异明显的策略纳入同一套研发与评测体系，包括采用自回归路线的 OpenVLA、采用 flow-matching 路线的 π0.5，以及 DiT4DiT、GR00T 等不同技术路线的模型。这意味着，统一工程框架不必以牺牲模型多样性为代价。FluxVLA 的模型接入并不局限于开放权重的模型。GPT-6 Astra 此前就以纯 API 的方式接入，同一套闭环评测，不提供权重、不参与训练，评测器照常跑完流程、留好证据。就在最新技术报告发布后两天，MiniMax-M3.1-Flash 成为继 GPT-6 Astra 之后第二个 checkpoint-free 的纯 API 推理策略，开箱即可在 LIBERO 与 RoboCasa GR1 上跑评测。数据层面也遵循同一套逻辑。不同机

articles.title: 华为群英传之刘睿：AI助手要告别聊天框，从“被动响应”走向“主动服务”
articles.content: 在商汤没做成的技术，登上了华为发布会。作者：李秋悦编辑：吴彤2022年6月，刘睿港中文博士毕业，赶上的却是一个“坏时候”。深度学习的高光已持续近十年，新突破越来越难；疫情之下，经济低迷，同届不少同学选择延期，再守一年实验室。刘睿没有等，他直接去了商汤。两个月后，Stable Diffusion发布；又过了三个月，ChatGPT引爆全球。刘睿毕业时以为正在退潮的世界，忽然换了一片海——商汤赖以生存的生意，为手机厂商定制算法、出售授权，开始松动；原本需要一个团队单独研发的算法，正被一个个基础模型收编。然后是2023年12月，汤晓鸥去世。“定海神针”突然离开，公司内部人心惶惶。刘睿也第一次认真想：汤老师不在了，商汤怎么办，自己怎么办。回头看，这个“坏时候”里埋着他此前人生的所有伏笔。2014年考入电子科技大学，他最初学光电子，很快觉得天地太窄；转入英才实验学院后，吴恩达的CS229让他迷上机器学习，李飞飞的CS231n把他领进深度学习和计算机视觉。2018年，他进入港中文MMLab，在王晓刚、李鸿升门下研究生成式模型——那正是几年后掀起巨浪的方向。从传统机器学习到深度学习，他几乎踩着AI最热闹的鼓点走完了求学路，却在毕业这年，听见鼓点停了。2024年，刘睿加入华为。这一次，他想换一种做技术的方式：不再把算法卖给客户，而是直接把它交到用户手里。此前在商汤未能立项的对话式修图，被他推上了2025年华为Mate 80的发布会；年底，小艺大模型应用实验室成立，刘睿出任首任主任，研究范围涵盖大语言模型、多模态智能、Agent与具身智能。做研究与做产品，在他手里第一次合流。也正是在这个时候，2022年那个“坏时候”显出了另一副面孔：如果他像同学一样延期一年、守在实验室里等风停，等来的不会是避风港，只会是又一场追赶。所谓坏时机，不过是旧浪退去、新浪未至的间隙——有人站在岸边等，有人先下了水。现在，刘睿关心的不再是追不追得上技术，而是另一个问题：模型能做的，和用户要的，之间还差什么。以下是雷峰网左林右狸频道与刘睿（华为小艺大型模型应用实验室创始主任）的对话，经编辑。01 商汤往事，大模型颠覆算法生意左林右狸频道：2018年，你在本科大四下学期去商汤科技研究院做实习生，是什么契机？刘睿：2017年7月，我参加香港中文大学MMLab的夏令营，认识了王晓刚、李鸿升、林达华几位老师。他们给我发了口头offer，我聊下来感觉也很好，决定明年去港中文MMLab读博。王晓刚、李鸿升老师觉得，做研究应该解决更有价值的工业界问题，所以建议我去商汤科技研究院实习，提前接受一些产业界的锻炼。左林右狸频道：当时面试你的人是闫俊杰。刘睿：俊杰这个人非常好，非常Nice，他是一个很有技术追求的人，也是我当时的mentor。但第一次面试时我对他的印象其实是他很sharp，面试体验也很特别，不会像其他面试官一样安安静静听你完整讲完一个工作，而是从一个点开始连环追问你，一直挖到触及你的知识盲区，再让你继续介绍工作。而且他抓重点非常精准，非常高效。十几分钟的连环问结束，他说欢迎来实习，就挂断了电话。左林右狸频道：在商汤科技研究院实习那小半年的时间，你在做什么工作？刘睿：当时主要做人脸识别研究。俊杰虽然是我的Mentor，但他从2015年加入商汤，一路从实习生做到总监，工作已经非常忙了，所以我更多是独立开展研究，向组里一些资深的研究员学习。这段实习有两个大收获，第一是接触到了大规模算力集群。当时商汤拥有非常丰富的GPU资源，我们可以一次性启动几百甚至上千张GPU训练人脸识别模型。我也是在那里学会了大规模GPU集群的使用。当时还处于深度学习时代，大家对算力重要性的认识没有今天这么深，但已经隐约感觉到，有算力的地方就有优势。第二是建立了产业界的Sense。此前我做研究，更多关注偏理论的问题。但在商汤，我逐渐意识到，真正有影响力的研究，应该解决实际的工业难题。这段经历也影响了我后来的研究选择，我一直希望自己做的技术能够解决真实的工业问题。左林右狸频道：2022年6月，你从港中文MMLab博士毕业，去商汤工作了两年？刘睿：我读博期间，王晓刚老师的主要精力已经逐渐往商汤迁移，我也受到王老师的影响，跟他所在的商汤部门有一些合作和联系。王老师主要负责牵引工业问题，李鸿升老师指导我具体的学术研究。毕业后，我算是顺理成章就加入了王老师负责的商汤MIG（Mobile Intelligence Group，移动智慧事业群）。当时MIG主要分终端和智驾两块，我在终端方向，主要为“华米OV”等手机厂商研发算法。同期合作比较多的是孙文秀和任思捷，俊杰当时已经离职创办MiniMax了。左林右狸频道：那两年你在干嘛？刘睿：我们当时做的事情很简单，就是尝试跟高通、联发科这些端侧芯片公司，包括索尼这样的半导体公司合作。因

articles.content:
arXiv:2610.35942v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: I consider what it means for AI assistance to save time. I contrast a stopwatch view, on which time saved is whatever the clock records, with a ledger view, on which it is a counterfactual that has to be read next to the errors the work lets through, and I argue for the latter. The argument has four parts. I define a model-free pair of quantities, time saved and excess escaped defects, and one decision number built from them: the break-even defect cost. I give a baseline model of checking in which, until the model is good enough not to check, a calibrated worker's escaped-defect rate does not depend on how good the model is; checking time grows with the logarithm of the model's error rate; and over-trust buys minutes on the clock at a larger cost in total minutes. Abstract: Multimodal intelligence can be viewed as human-guided co-evolution between worlds and agents through interaction. We therefore introduce The Trinity, a recursive self-improvement framework coupling world generation with Harness evolution through three roles: Creator, Explorer, and Evolver. articles.title: Why and How to Do Science When AI Is Better at It: A Framework Grounded in Human Understanding and Direction
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36116v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: As AI begins to match or exceed human researchers at core scientific tasks, two questions become pressing: \emph{why} should humans keep doing science, and \emph{how} should they use AI when they do? This paper argues that the second can be answered only by answering the first. It holds that one indispensable aim of science is \emph{durable, collective human understanding of the world, pursued in service of human ends and values}. From this principle it derives a two-part test for when a research task can be delegated to AI. The first part, \emph{human understanding}, requires that the scientific community remain able to explain, defend and contest the resulting claims, and retain the skills to do so. The second, \emph{human direction}, requires that judgments about which questions matter and what findings mean stay with accountable humans. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36146v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Prompt optimization should improve the image a user receives without changing the scene the user requested. Yet stylistic rewriting can weaken object attributes and relations even when global text--image similarity remains high. We propose StruPO, a structure-aware prompt editor that uses a calibrated scene graph as a shared representation for policy conditioning and image-grounded supervision. The graph exposes what should be preserved, while deletion, reordering, and insertion provide a token-aligned way to modify the prompt. This turns structural feedback from an external critique into a training signal for a reusable editing policy. Learning from that signal requires handling both uncertain grounding and stochastic image generation. StruPO retains grounding confidence through smooth reward shaping and averages multiple images for each edit before computing group-relative advantages. articles.title: Don't Pick a Winner: Knowledge Conflicts Need a Prior, Not a Rule
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36169v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A retrieval-augmented language model answers from two sources, the retrieved context and its own knowledge, and the two disagree whenever the context is incomplete or wrong. Existing methods settle the disagreement with a rule fixed at design time: follow the context, amplify it in proportion to how far it moves the model, or trust the model's memory. Each rule is confidently wrong in some deployment. In a decision-theoretic model of two sources, the score of any fixed rule is linear in the share of reliable contexts while the best attainable score is convex, so every fixed rule is beaten wherever it is not exactly optimal; and a symmetric divergence between the two sources, the signal adaptive decoding uses, carries no information about which one is right. Abstract: We study time-to-arrival (TTA) in sports: the shortest plausible time a player needs to reach an arbitrary location on the pitch given their current kinematic state, estimated as the lower envelope of observed locomotion times. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36188v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly rely on reusable skills for complex software engineering tasks, making skill libraries essential for repository development and maintenance. However, repository-specific skills must evolve with changing code structures, implementation conventions, and maintenance requirements. Pull requests (PRs) provide a natural source of such knowledge by recording how repositories evolve through implementation and review. Meanwhile, new PRs must follow repository-specific implementation patterns, modify related components consistently, and ensure that existing tests continue to pass while adding coverage for new functionality. This creates a mutually reinforcing cycle: PRs provide knowledge for updating skills, while these skills improve future PRs, maintain repositories, and support further skill evolution. Abstract: Requirements engineering (RE) is foundational to systems engineering (SE), as requirement defects can propagate downstream and adversely affect development outcomes. Although large language models (LLMs) are promising for requirement quality assessment, prior work shows that off-the-shelf models miss a large share of expert-identified defects, perform unevenly across quality criteria, and vary across executions. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36298v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Machine learning models deployed behind query interfaces expose more than their predictions, because an adversary can use those predictions to rebuild the model itself. Model stealing attacks (MSAs) exploit this exposure by training a surrogate model that replicates the decision behavior of a target through black-box queries alone, without access to its parameters or training data. These attacks are well characterized for conventional artificial neural networks (ANNs), yet spiking neural networks (SNNs) process information in a fundamentally different way. SNNs communicate through sparse, discrete spikes, and their outputs depend on membrane potentials that evolve over time rather than on a static mapping from input to output. This temporal mode of computation suggests that the decision behavior of an SNN may be harder to reconstruct from its responses. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36335v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) perform well across many real-world tasks but remain prone to hallucination, limiting their reliability in domains such as biomedicine and healthcare, where answers must be grounded in established knowledge. Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) mitigates this problem by incorporating external information, but often overlooks logical relationships and relies heavily on the LLM's own reasoning, which can compromise answer faithfulness. We propose OA-RAG, an agent that integrates formal reasoning with LLM reasoning, drawing on both the logical structure and informal annotations of domain ontologies. For each answer, OA-RAG reports the ontology observations used as evidence and a model-assessed grounding level (entailed, supported, related, or unrelated) that characterises the strength of that evidence. Abstract: Data stream classification under concept drift and class imbalance requires models to adapt continuously while maintaining strong minority-class performance. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.33133v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The drift-diffusion equations are the fundamental building block for the modeling, design, and optimization of modern semiconductor devices. Solutions of the drift-diffusion equations rarely give way to analytical forms, and exhibit strong nonlinearity, with the solutions ranging over several orders of magnitude. These attributes have led to research into numerical solvers, and while many commercial Technology Computer Aided Design (TCAD) packages now exist, they may require long simulation times, exhibit sensitivity to initial guesses, and rely on mesh generation. Further, these solvers are not well suited for inverse problems where the design parameters of a device are retrieved from its desired functional characteristics. Abstract: Understanding how neural activity encodes behavioral and sensory variables is a key challenge in systems neuroscience. articles.content:

Abstract: Deep learning architectures tend to generalize well to unseen data, but explaining this capability is still an open area of research. Under the assumption of i.i.d. data, PAC-Bayes provides a bound on generalization error, and its tightness relies on a parameter distribution that covers a large volume of low-loss solutions. Abstract: Multivariable time series forecasting plays an important role in various domains, where predictions depend on complex interactions among covariates. Forecasting models are commonly evaluated across numerous benchmark datasets. However, forecasting accuracy reflects both model capability and task predictability, making it difficult to characterise the difficulty of a task independently of the model used. In this work, we propose Multivariable Predictability Score (MAPS), a model-agnostic metric for measuring the intrinsic predictability of multivariable time series forecasting tasks. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.33215v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large vision-language models (VLMs), which process both visual inputs and text queries, incur high inference costs due to the large number of visual tokens, making visual token pruning a natural approach for improving efficiency. Recent work has leveraged query information to guide token selection, often through heuristics derived from attention patterns or token dynamics. However, these approaches do not explicitly exploit the underlying structure of query-vision interactions. We address this gap by observing that the query-vision interaction matrix, naturally induced by the query and key projections already present in transformer attention, is effectively low-rank, with a small number of dominant latent interaction modes capturing query-relevant semantics. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.33217v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Activation steering is a popular approach for shifting LLM output toward a desired behavior, and increasingly for generating realistic synthetic data. The standard recipe estimates a steering direction by contrasting LLM activations on prompts with and without a target concept, such as truthfulness. In this paper, we separate the estimand (the steering direction these methods target) from the estimator used to recover it, two notions the literature often conflates. We frame nearly all existing methods as plug-in estimators of the average gradient of an outcome regression, with the binary contrastive label fixed as the outcome. Using this framing, we can immediately incorporate flexible modeling approaches and extend existing methods to allow for continuous outcomes such as log-probabilities or oracle ratings. Abstract: Auto-bidding systems in online advertising must balance competing objectives-maximizing budget delivery while minimizing cost per action-across heterogeneous campaigns under non-stationary market conditions. This trade-off evolves over campaign lifespans: early on, cost optimization dominates when budgets roll over; near deadlines, budget delivery becomes urgent. While PID controllers are widely used in production for their stability and interpretability, fixed tunings cannot adapt to diverse campaigns and shifting traffic patterns. Abstract: Classical optimization and learning-guided search offer complementary approaches to open problems in discrete mathematics, but their outputs are difficult to compare when search spaces, validity checks, and stopping rules differ. We present \emph{RadonBench}, a benchmark for constructing maximum-cardinality Radon-free lattice configurations: finite subsets of $\mathbb{Z}^d$ admitting no integral Radon partition. It remains open whether Radon-free configurations with $11$ points in $\mathbb{Z}^3$ or $21$ points in $\mathbb{Z}^4$ are possible. If they exist, they would improve the corresponding lower bounds on the integer Radon numbers. We compare exhaustive extension, greedy local search, PatternBoost, AlphaZero, and AlphaEvolve. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.33285v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Individual fairness in machine learning requires that similar individuals receive similar predictions. Most existing definitions are pairwise in nature, imposing a Lipschitz constraint that must hold either globally across all pairs of data instances or locally within specified neighborhoods. In practice, however, such pairwise constraints may be overly restrictive and may not directly identify which individuals receive locally inconsistent predictions. We study local predictive consistency as a node-level relaxation of pairwise individual fairness, where each prediction is compared with a similarity-weighted average of predictions in its local neighborhood. This yields an interpretable node-level fairness score and a corresponding regularized learning approach based on local residuals. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.33298v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Quantization, pruning, and model merging are popular transformations applied to deployment-ready LLMs to improve efficiency and downstream performance. Recent work has shown that these transformations can introduce a security threat: an adversary can train a model that passes safety checks in its pre-transformed state, only turning malicious once it is transformed for deployment. However, prior attacks target one specific transformation (e.g., quantization) and generally rely on transformation-specific techniques, making them difficult to combine in practice. In this work, we introduce a simple, composable attack framework that targets multiple transformations simultaneously and triggers when any one of them is applied by a user. articles.title: Tree Depth and Sample-Quality-Associated Features: Two Hidden Factors in Boruta Selection for RNA-Seq Data Classification
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.33307v2 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Boruta is a widely used method for selecting gene panels from RNA sequencing data, and its most used implementation recommends Random Forest trees of depth 3 to 7, an untested setting. We tested whether this setting changes which genes are selected, using pan-cancer data from The Cancer Genome Atlas (10,469 tumors, 33 cancer types) and breast cancer PAM50 subtyping (981 tumors, 5 subtypes). A leakage-free protocol fitted every label-dependent step inside training folds, measured every effect against seed-to-seed variation, and held out a locked test set per task. In pan-cancer data, shallow trees changed the selection far more than a new seed did: the top-500 overlap with unlimited-depth selections was 0.37 at depth 5, against 0.84 to 0.93 between seeds at depth 5 or unlimited depth. Shallow trees confirmed 3.5 times fewer genes, missed markers of large classes and produced less accurate 50-gene panels (balanced accuracy 0.809 vs 0.889).

articles.content:
arXiv:2610.33315v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Diffusion models have become a dominant approach to structure-based drug design. However, because they are trained primarily to fit reference structures, they often place ligands in physically implausible poses that clash with the protein. We introduce MLIPDiff, an inference-time guidance method that can be applied to pretrained diffusion models for ligand generation. The method uses physics-informed guidance from UMA (Universal Models for Atoms), a machine-learned interatomic potential (MLIP). The guidance combines four weighted energy terms (protein-ligand interaction, ligand strain, steric clash, and pocket anchoring) and uses the original model checkpoint without retraining. Abstract: Adversarial training remains one of the most effective defenses against adversarial attacks, but its standard PGD-based training is computationally expensive because adversarial examples are generated for every training sample. Selective adversarial training reduces this cost by perturbing only a subset of samples. Abstract: Training contextual masking systems for personally identifiable information (PII) requires examples distinguishing maskable from preservable mentions of one entity type, but privacy restrictions limit access to real data. Author-based augmentation (SPY) labels mentions unrelated to the author as non-PII, presuming a single data subject and overlooking others. Abstract: System One decision models such as Jev answer structured questions in a single forward pass without generating text, offering fast and computationally efficient clinical decision support. Abstract: General-purpose embodied intelligence requires robots to coordinate diverse skills over long horizons, track task progress, and recover from failures. Our progressive training framework combines embodied pretraining, domain-specialized agent distillation, and multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD). Abstract: Election integrity is a shared commitment in American politics, but Democrats and Republicans in Congress increasingly mean different things by it. Using diachronic word embeddings, which track semantic change through how words are used in context, we measure how differently each party uses each term, how much each party shifts, and whether they share nearest semantic neighbors. We show that members of Congress do not need different words to tell different stories about elections. They need only place those same words in different company. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36230v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: IceBERT, the reference encoder for Icelandic, found that a cleaned web crawl is enough to train a strong model and that starting from a multilingual model can help on some tasks. We revisit both findings with the ModernBERT architecture. We train Icelandic encoders from 12M to 1B parameters on 9B tokens of open data, and rerun IceBERT's benchmarks and five newer tasks for 30 encoders under one protocol with confidence intervals. Our 1B model trained from scratch, to our knowledge the first monolingual Icelandic encoder of that size, is significantly better than IceBERT on all eleven tasks; warm-started from the English Ettin encoder of the same shape, it has the best score of all encoders on every task we rank. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36353v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) often answer ambiguous inputs as if they had a single intended meaning. This is problematic because input ambiguity is an upstream source of uncertainty: when a prompt admits multiple valid interpretations, the key question is whether the model should answer directly at all. Existing input uncertainty methods often rely on LLM-generated statements or clarifications, but such transformations may already disambiguate the input before the ambiguity is measured. We propose a label-preserving perturbation framework for input ambiguity detection in which perturbations remain close to the original input while preserving its label. We instantiate this principle with two detectors: a black-box rule-based perturbation library and a white-box importance-guided method using model-internal signals. Abstract: We present AK_QMUL's submissions to the ArGuard-2026 shared tasks on Arabic harmful-prompt detection: a binary safe/unsafe task (B1) and a seven-way harm-domain task (B2). Both submissions use one backbone -- JAIS-6.7B fine-tuned with 4-bit QLoRA and a linear classification head over its last-token representation. For B2 we fine-tune the same backbone as a seven-way classifier and average the softmax outputs of five random seeds. Both submissions ranked first on their track, with macro-F1 0.984 on B1 and 0.790 on B2. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36432v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Homoglyph and invisible-character watermarks are edit-based watermarks. Instead of changing how a model generates text, they hide a signal in the text after it is written. They swap some characters for homoglyphs, which look the same, or very similar, but have different Unicode code points, or they insert characters that do not display, all without access to the model that wrote the text. Generation-time watermarks work less well for lower-resourced languages due to how tokenizers split their text. Because they work on individual characters, these watermarks never touch a tokenizer, so we ask whether they escape this gap. Across 40 language varieties in 24 scripts, we measure capacity (the hidden bits each character can carry), how much of it survives routine handling and targeted removal, and how much text a keyed detector needs. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36437v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: When a Large Language Model (LLM) is trained with Reinforcement Learning (RL) on multiple tasks, a task's primary reward can gate auxiliary rewards such as a length reward: on a failing response, an auxiliary cannot exceed the primary. However, group-relative advantage estimators treat a gated auxiliary like any other component, so it can reverse the primary's order, and at the primary's ceiling only auxiliaries order responses. Keeping gated auxiliaries hurts some tasks, while dropping them hurts others. We propose CONCUR, an advantage estimator that replaces the standardized scores of each gated auxiliary with the closest scores that satisfy two conditions: responses with higher primary rewards cannot receive lower scores, and responses at the primary's ceiling receive equal scores. articles.title: Do AI Scientists Know What's New?
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36511v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A major challenge facing AI scientific discovery pipelines is how to determine when a generated idea is meaningfully novel. Ideally, novelty checks in these pipelines must be able to reject non-novel ideas while not rejecting too many novel ideas, and they should also be able to distinguish which parts of a proposal are non-novel, as opposed to opaquely discarding entire proposals. We design an analytical framework for evaluation of novelty checks with temporal ground truth at both the proposal- and claim-level, using four datasets of 1,060 proposals built from published papers, reviewer disputes, and generated ideas matching ones the field went on to publish. Evaluating this transition requires connecting the information preserved at handoff to how the receiver continues the work, a relationship that task-success and memory-retention scores alone do not capture. Abstract: Written transcripts of the same speech can differ in ways that are not uniquely determined by the speech signal. We formulate evaluation-side transcript canonicalization (ETC), which maps multiple surface forms to a single canonical form when their differences are not determined by speech. To our knowledge, ETC-Bench is the first and most comprehensive multilingual benchmark for evaluation-side transcript canonicalization, covering 181 phenomenon types across 12 languages. Each instance is a minimal pair that shares a sentence context and differs only in a target span exhibiting one phenomenon. To evaluate both canonicalization success and semantic preservation, we propose Semantic-preserving Exact-match Normalization Accuracy (SENA), which combines exact agreement between independently canonicalized pair members with a pair-relative BERTScore constraint against information loss. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36538v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Multilingual automatic speech recognition (ASR) has achieved rapid progress with large-scale pretrained models and multilingual speech corpora. Previous studies have proved the pivotal role of data sampling in multilingual ASR performance. However, existing sampling strategies largely rely on time-consuming manual, heuristic-based designs. To address this, we propose a linguistic-aware agentic data sampling framework that introduces a data sampling LLM agent into the multilingual ASR training loop. The agent is driven by a linguistically grounded rubric that analyzes ASR errors from phonological, morphological, and syntactic perspectives, and uses the resulting feedback together with training statistics, budget constraints, and algorithm profiles to select domain-level, sample-level, and token-level sampling strategies. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36582v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: To generate landmark-based route instructions, models must understand both map geometry and human landmark preferences. Although large language models (LLMs) show great abilities in language tasks, the best way to structure map data for these models is not yet established. This paper proposes a structured text representation for landmark selection tasks in route navigation, utilizing SVG format to encode spatial features. The structured text maintains a geometric connection with rendered map images, allowing language models to directly access spatial and semantic data. Using a new dataset created from human-written route descriptions and OpenStreetMap data, we evaluate models on two tasks: landmark selection at turns and around destinations. Abstract: Discourse parsing based on Segmented Discourse Representation Theory (SDRT) is crucial for capturing the structural dynamics of dialogues. However, most prior research focuses on English, and its effectiveness for Japanese remains unclear owing to the lack of Japanese SDRT corpora. To address this issue, we construct Japanese SDRT corpora by translating existing English SDRT corpora using an LLM. Through a comparative evaluation of prompt-based and fine-tuned LLMs, we show that the models achieve comparable performance between English and Japanese, suggesting the cross-lingual applicability of SDRT-based discourse parsing. Abstract: Image quality assessment (IQA) underpins embodied imaging pipelines by judging whether visual quality satisfies downstream tasks, yet most existing methods learn task-agnostic scores aligned with generic human ratings on static benchmarks. This objective mismatches embodied and interactive settings, where image adequacy depends on task goals, context, and action requirements that shape an agent's decisions. We argue that IQA should shift from score regression to goal-conditioned judgment defined by embodied task utility. To this end, we propose an MLLM-based embodied IQA agent framework that reasons about task requirements, grounds quality evidence, and produces decision-facing assessments. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.35910v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Emergent generative AI technologies, while remarkably beneficial across several tasks and domains, can suffer from unforeseen vulnerabilities and difficult-to-anticipate failure modes. Such failure modes can disparately affect vulnerable communities. This paper investigates two well-known vision language models (VLMs) and inspects how these models encode protected identities while generating images. We show that when VLMs are requested to transform human face images to reflect race identities (e.g., Hispanic, Black, White, or Asian) and sexual orientation (e.g., gay or straight), VLMs often comply with such requests. We demonstrate that compliance (and refusal) is non-deterministic, group-sensitive, and generated images are statistically distinguishable, often accentuating deep-seated stereotypes. Abstract: Image and video generators can produce spatially consistent visual content, but how to use this capability to improve spatial understanding remains underexplored. To this end, we introduce a unified geometric understanding and generation model (GeoUG) that integrates depth and multi-view generation with spatial understanding. First, we design a multi-scale depth codec that enables metric-depth generation using a pretrained visual autoencoder, and show that joint training yields task-dependent gains in spatial understanding. Abstract: Geometry foundation models recover camera poses and dense geometry from a set of images with a feed-forward network, but they expect pinhole images. Abstract: Despite rapid progress in visual understanding and document transcription, modern vision-language models (VLMs) struggle with a fundamental accessibility task: reading Braille from images. We introduce BrailleBench, a manually curated benchmark of 259 real-world Grade-1 and Grade-2 Braille images. Abstract: Video Large Language Models (VLMs) have demonstrated strong capabilities in video understanding and reasoning, but processing long visual sequences incurs substantial computational, latency, and memory overhead. This survey examines training-free inference acceleration, focusing on reducing inference costs while preserving task-relevant spatiotemporal evidence. We organize existing methods by their intervention stages in the inference pipeline, covering input, visual encoding, projector, prefill, and decoding. Post-training quantization (PTQ) is discussed separately as a cross-stage extension with varying calibration requirements. We analyze how intervention position affects evidence preservation and computational savings, and why local efficiency improvements may not translate into end-to-end acceleration. Abstract: Multi-task learning (MTL) improves model efficiency by sharing representations across related vision tasks, but it often suffers from negative transfer when task updates interfere with one another. Abstract: Crowd-counting models deployed on edge devices face two shifts: inputs are degraded along the capture and transmission pipeline, while models are quantized to satisfy resource constraints. The corruptions span six families, with head annotations adjusted when geometry or visibility changes. articles.title: BoxWorld: Let World Engines Control and Video Generators Render
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36371v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We tackle the challenge of building real-time interactive video worlds with user-defined behaviors. Such worlds must track object states, apply interaction rules, and render the resulting consequences as users act. Yet existing end-to-end video world models typically learn interaction dynamics within the generator, making it difficult to specify object-level rules and reason about their consequences. In this work, we introduce BoxWorld, which separates interaction reasoning from generative rendering. Given user-specified rules, a coding agent creates a Box World Engine that determines interaction outcomes and exposes the resulting object states through a lightweight interface of layout boxes, persistent object attributes, and dynamic status variables, leaving appearance and physical effects to generative rendering. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36379v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) shows promise for breast imaging, but limited labeled data, institutional data fragmentation, and privacy concerns hinder centralized training. We investigate a privacy-aware federated learning framework combining pretrained vision-language models (VLMs) with client-level differential privacy. We compare general-purpose CLIP models, biomedical BiomedCLIP, and an ImageNet-pretrained ViT-B/16 baseline on two public breast imaging datasets, with and without differential privacy. We also evaluate a CLIP ViT-B/16 ablation that removes the text pathway. Evaluation includes patient-level ROC-AUC with bootstrap 95% confidence intervals, baseline comparisons, threshold sensitivity, inter-model agreement, and communication cost. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36384v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Perceiving human body motion is critical for multimodal systems that understand and assist people. Yet current evaluations of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) largely focus on objects, scenes, and coarse actions, leaving their ability to reason about the body itself poorly assessed. This is especially challenging from the egocentric perspective, in which the body is only partially visible and motion must be inferred from occluded and temporally distributed cues. We introduce SOMA, a benchmark for fine-grained body-motion understanding from egocentric video, comprising 1,632 human-verified questions across three capability axes: body configuration, motion dynamics, and temporal reasoning. We evaluate 37 leading closed-source, open-source, and specialized egocentric MLLMs, complemented by an extensive human evaluation. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36411v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Compact electroencephalography (EEG) decoders enable embedded brain--computer interfaces (BCIs), but compression can alter adversarial robustness without proportional hardware savings. We present ORBITAL, a robustness-constrained framework combining hardware-realizable structured compression, recovery-aware operating-point selection, multi-attack evaluation, and native edge validation. Matched controls identify TRADES as the main source of robustness recovery, improving S25 union accuracy by 6.74 percentage points over clean recovery (p=0.0039), while per-example analysis reveals boundary redistribution rather than uniform margin expansion. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36419v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present Scalable Pixel-anchored End-to-end Diffusion (SpeeDiff), a latent diffusion method that jointly trains the VAE and the diffusion model from scratch. In principle, joint training allows the diffusion loss gradient to directly guide the VAE encoder, encouraging the formation of a generation-friendly latent space and potentially yielding faster convergence than the conventional two-stage approach with a pretrained frozen VAE. However, a naive end-to-end implementation severely degrades performance, as unrestricted backpropagation of the diffusion loss leads to latent space collapse. Our main technical contribution is a simple yet effective Tweedie Pixel Reconstruction (TPR) loss, which provides additional pixel-level feedback by decoding a predicted clean latent from an intermediate noisy state using Tweedie's formula, thereby alleviating collapse. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36011v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: World-action models (WAMs) offer a promising framework for embodied intelligence, yet mainstream approaches remain centered on video foundation models or vision-language models. Even when geometric features extracted by 3D models such as VGGT are incorporated, they are typically passed into a video model or VLM that serves as the primary backbone, leaving 3D geometry as an auxiliary input or prediction target rather than the native foundation for world modeling. First, it adopts a 3D foundation model as the primary backbone, making 3D geometry the native representation for both world modeling and action prediction. articles.title: Rollback: Experience Backtracking in World Models for Policy Improvement
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36068v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Action-conditioned world models offer a scalable alternative to costly real-world interaction for improving robot policies. However, existing world-model-based methods largely treat world models as forward-only surrogates of the physical environment, leaving untapped a capability no physical environment affords: rewinding to past decision points to explore counterfactual futures. We introduce Rollback, a policy improvement paradigm that turns world models from passive simulators into counterfactual engines: it rolls back to critical decision points, branches into alternative actions, and contrasts their outcomes to attribute success to individual decisions. This concentrates imagination where it matters most and distills counterfactual outcomes into fine-grained, action-level supervision without a separately learned value model. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36079v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: End-to-end autonomous driving has predominantly relied on open-loop imitation learning for training, which presents two limitations. First, expert demonstrations show only one behavior per scenario, so the model cannot learn alternative valid behaviors and, in turn, cannot adapt to user-specified preferences at test time. Second, noise or ambiguity in these demonstrations can produce inconsistent, unreliable supervision for the end-to-end models. Driving is inherently multi-modal: multiple different behaviors can be valid responses to the same scene, and this diversity arises largely from speed rather than path. We introduce a planning paradigm that learns the path through imitation while scoring a set of candidate speeds across multiple criteria with a learned function supervised by physically grounded safety constraints. articles.title: Program-Level Adversarial Co-Adaptive Self-Play for Robotic Security
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36143v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Coding agents can adapt robotic software by revising executable programs, but successful responses to an evolving opponent may not remain effective. We present a framework for program-level adversarial co-adaptive self-play in which coding agents generate attacks and defenses from tested opponent code and mission feedback, without model fine-tuning. Environment-specific interfaces support external programs for autonomous driving and SDK-level defenses for humanoid locomotion. Two eight-generation case studies reveal concrete software responses: a driving defender introduces direct-actuation recovery, while a humanoid defender revises incoming-state validation. These responses provide local task recovery but do not establish sustained robustness. The framework makes such adaptation and limitations observable through executable artifacts and task-level evidence.

articles.title: cuArms: GPU-Accelerated Conflict-Based Planning for Multi-Arm Manipulation
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36250v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Multi-arm manipulation has the potential to dramatically improve the throughput, efficiency, and dexterity of many manipulation tasks. Recent work coordinates multiple robot arms in a shared workcell by allocating and scheduling tasks for greater parallelism, jointly planning multi-arm motions, or directly learning multi-arm policies. So far, these approaches are either too slow, rely on domain-specific assumptions, or scale poorly with the number of robots and task horizon. Thus, we introduce cuArms, a conflict-based planner co-designed with GPU parallelism that efficiently decomposes the search space using reusable multi-modal roadmaps for individual robots and resolves conflicts and deadlocks through a lazy search. To jointly optimize task assignment, schedules, motions, and manipulation skills, we integrate a high-level scheduler that proposes candidate skeletons for cuArms to ground into coordinated manipulation plans. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36270v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Complex whole-body loco-manipulation requires executing diverse maneuvers, such as crouching, grasping, and locomotion, within a single long-horizon task. While performing simple pick-and-place behaviors is well-established, scaling to complex, long-horizon tasks remains difficult. Currently, this challenge is addressed by relying on human motion data and correspondingly humanoid platforms, which limits platform independence and introduces substantial data processing overhead. Instead, we extend proximal policy optimization (PPO) to train a single policy for multi-phase tasks across diverse robotic hardware, leveraging prior task structure to shape behavior. Our method adapts PPO using a phase-conditioned critic, phase-gated reward functions, and a multi-phase reset curriculum to guide exploration. articles.title: ASPEN: Adaptive Semantic Reasoning via Command Persistence Prediction for Efficient Navigation VLAs
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36285v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Navigation vision-language-action (VLA) policies repeatedly invoke costly semantic reasoning even when the next command remains unchanged. Command reuse can reduce computation but risks missing instruction-dependent turns or stops. We introduce ASPEN, an event-triggered scheduler based on command persistence prediction: estimating whether the frozen base policy would reissue its previous command. A lightweight multimodal predictor combines temporal observations, language instructions, execution history, and cached VLA confidence. At eligible command boundaries, sufficient predicted persistence permits command reuse. Otherwise, ASPEN triggers fresh semantic reasoning from the VLA. Evaluated with frozen NaVILA on cross-dataset RxR-CE val-unseen, ASPEN reduces VLA calls by 9.5% and estimated inference time by 8.1%, including scheduling overhead. It maintains comparable navigation performance and preserves identical baseline action sequences

articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36312v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Monocular outdoor navigation requires robust camera motion estimation and a dense, navigable map, where 3D Gaussian Splatting SLAM serves this task through an explicit differentiable parameterization and closed-form projection. However, typically, the geometry is recovered by associating 2D pixels with 3D points, so a modular SLAM system absorbs tracking error into the map, leading to cascading degradation. To address these gaps, we present SG^2SLAM, which couples streaming spatial geometry with a ray-conditioned 3DGS kernel. Streaming spatial geometry replaces the per- frame cross-dimensional correspondence with a chunk-level metric prior that supervises tracking and mapping from one source. A ray-conditioned kernel extends each primitive with a viewing-direction subspace that senses the monocular camera viewpoints. articles.title: HIDRA: Hierarchical Dual-Routing Attention for Replay-Free Lifelong Imitation Learning
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36374v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Robotic agents operating in real-world environments must adapt continuously from a stream of multimodal demonstrations, often under constraints that preclude storing or revisiting past data. In this replay-free, single-pass lifelong imitation learning setting, sequential updates can progressively distort the representation space, making expert-based approaches particularly sensitive to routing interference, causing expert selection to degrade over time. We propose HIDRA, a structured routing framework that mitigates this issue through a hierarchical dual-attention mechanism, which decouples instruction-level expert retrieval from context-dependent refinement. To further stabilize routing under representation drift, HIDRA introduces a key-level geometric regularization that enforces both alignment within tasks and separation across tasks. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36407v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: TrackJoint is a Modelica MultiBody component that turns a three-dimensional road surface into a joint with two degrees of freedom. The two joint coordinates are the distance travelled along a reference line and the sideways offset from that line. Together they give the position, orientation and angular velocity of a single frame_b connector. All road geometry reaches the joint as a small set of periodic piecewise-quintic splines, so one component can represent any circuit whose splines have been fitted beforehand. The road constraint is closed with d'Alembert's principle. The two generalized forces that belong to the joint coordinates are set to zero, so no Lagrange multipliers are needed. The joint is connected to a multibody race car in Dymola and the pair is exported as one FMI~3.0 FMU. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36430v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A track fitting pipeline is presented that converts a measured racetrack point cloud into a closed, $C^4$ differentiable, three-dimensional surface model suitable for high-fidelity Modelica race-car optimization. The surface is a Monge patch, parametrised by a curvilinear arc-length coordinate measured along the minimum-curvature line (MCL) and a signed lateral offset, with a height polynomial of user-selectable degree capturing the cross-sectional elevation profile. Abstract: As expansion and scalability in underwater oper- ations becomes more important and challenging, autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) become more relevant and the necessity for reliable autonomy more critical. Abstract: Humanoid behavior foundation models (BFMs) provide reusable whole-body motion priors: given a kinematic reference, they generate coordinated joint commands for motion replay, teleoperation, and VLA control. Abstract: Recently, LLM-based autonomous agents have shown strong capabilities in iteratively generating, evaluating, and refining executable solutions. However, effective program search requires physical understanding: agents must understand how objects can be manipulated, how scene geometry constrains actions, and why interactions succeed or fail. Abstract: Differences in musculoskeletal morphology challenge policy reuse across individual models. Here we present MyoAcross, a framework that combines individual musculoskeletal model construction, morphology-conditioned policy learning and virtual model augmentation to enable muscle-driven reference-motion tracking without individual fine-tuning. Policy reuse extends to models of 22 held-out individuals constructed from single-image shape estimates, measured height and body mass, and, with asymmetry augmentation, to models with unilateral lower-limb shortening. Abstract: We present CPG-ENN, a trainable quadruped locomotion framework that combines explicit neural coordination with learned motion realization. A symmetry-based eight-neuron central pattern generator (CPG) supplies gait rhythms, while a pretrained, leg-shared execution neural network (ENN) maps rhythmic signals and trajectory parameters to joint-angle references without online inverse kinematics. A single feedback policy modulates six physically interpretable trajectory variables. The controller tracks planar velocity and yaw-rate commands across walk, trot, pace, bound, and pronk without gait-specific learned controllers or transitionspecific rewards. Simulation yields 99.39% transition success across all 20 directed gait pairs and all source-target speed combinations from {0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0} m/s. articles.content:

Abstract: Humans are dexterous, but traditional data collection paradigms such as teleoperation, kinesthetic teaching, and wearable exoskeletons force humans to act through the robot embodiment, bottlenecking their dexterity. Retargeting can avoid this. However, existing methods purely translate kinematics and ignore the real-world contact dynamics essential for task success. We present CARD: Contact-Anchored Retargeting for Dexterous Manipulation, a simulator and object-free framework that retargets human demonstrations to robot actions by explicitly preserving contact force targets. CARD unifies human data sources including video, motion capture, and tactile gloves via a shared hand--contact representation and generates explicit contact force targets in addition to kinematics. articles.title: REACH: An RL-based Hierarchical Humanoid Crawling Framework for Adaptable Confined Space Traversal
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36546v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Humanoid locomotion in confined spaces requires continuous height adaptation across multiple locomotion modes, yet most existing approaches remain limited to height-adjustable bipedal walking. We present REACH, an RL-based hierarchical framework that enables a Unitree G1 humanoid to traverse height-constrained environments through variable-height bipedal walking and crawling. The learned policies regulate body height over complementary command ranges of 1.27--0.50m in bipedal locomotion and 0.50--0.20m in crawling, extending traversal beyond the clearance limits of crouched walking. To address contact-rich crawling dynamics, we employ a history-conditioned latent representation that captures terrain and interaction context from proprioceptive observations. articles.title: AI做中学 创未来｜智源SoulAgent持续拓展教育应用
articles.content: 10月19日至24日，北京智源人工智能研究院（以下简称“智源研究院”）连续走进中国人民大学附属中学，先后支持北京市“做中学”领航行动海淀区工作部署会暨科学与工程实践研讨会、“AI做中学，创未来——人工智能赋能创新人才培养研讨会”等活动，围绕SoulAgent在真实课堂、教研和学习场景中的应用开展实践与交流。 SoulAgent是智源研究院推出的“越用越懂你的个人智能体”。在教育场景中，SoulAgent围绕“帮我听课”、教师AI分身、作文批改、教学答疑等方向，探索AI如何帮助教师提升教学效率、沉淀教学内容，同时通过反馈、追问等方式支持学生理解问题、拓展思路、持续思考。 图注：SoulAgent走进校园，围绕真实教学与学习场景开展应用实践。 “帮我听课”：同时听多堂课，让课堂内容持续服务教研公开课、听课和教研等场景中，多门课程往往同时进行，教师既需要关注课堂现场，也要记录内容、梳理重点并完成课后复盘，有限的时间很难兼顾所有感兴趣的课程。SoulAgent“帮我听课”通过AI速记、智能总结和持续问答，辅助记录课堂内容、梳理教学重点。即使无法进入每一间课堂，教师也可以在课后回顾感兴趣的课程，并围绕课堂内容继续提问，让“听课”不再受限于同一时间只能进入一间教室。 10月21日活动期间，27节公开课接入SoulAgent“帮我听课”，通过课堂文字整理、教学要点梳理等功能，为教师回顾课堂、开展教学复盘提供参考。当天上午多门研究课并行开展，下午随即进入7个教研分论坛，沉淀下来的课堂速记和总结也可以成为后续讨论的共同参考，减少对课堂内容的重复回顾，把更多时间用于教学分析、经验交流和深入研讨。 从课堂记录到课后追问，再到教学复盘和教研交流，SoulAgent希望让一次性的课堂内容进一步沉淀为可查询、可回顾、可持续使用的教学资源。  图注：SoulAgent通过课堂文字整理、教学要点梳理和持续问答，为教师回顾课堂和开展教学复盘提供参考。教师AI分身：让AI先理解教师，再辅助教学如果说“帮我听课”解决的是课堂信息如何被更高效地记录和使用，那么教师AI分身进一步面对的，是AI如何真正适应不同教师的教学方式。 不同教师有自己的课程设计、评价尺度、批注习惯和讲评重点，真实教学并不存在一套完全统一的标准。SoulAgent将教师的课程资料、评价标准、批注样例、讲评口径以及实际使用中的反馈持续沉淀，形成专属教师分身。在此基础上，教师AI分身可以按照具体教师的专业标准，辅助完成作文批改、课堂总结、教学答疑等任务，并在持续使用中逐步贴近教师本人的评价尺度和教学方式。 因此，教师AI分身并不是为所有教师提供同一套“标准答案”，而是将教师自己的知识、经验和专业标准沉淀下来，让AI先理解教师，再按照教师的要求提供辅助。   从教师AI分身到英语作文批改，进入真实教学任务在英语作文批改场景中，教师提供评分标准、批注样例、讲评材料等专业依据，SoulAgent教师AI分身将这些教学标准带入具体批改任务，一个班级的个性化批改报告可以快速生成。 在实际应用中，SoulAgent教师AI分身可以根据具体教学需求，为学生提供更有针对性的修改建议，同时辅助教师梳理班级共性问题、典型案例和改进方向，并将有价值的内容持续沉淀，用于后续讲评、备课和教学。 对学生而言，反馈从一个分数进一步走向具体的问题分析和修改建议；对教师而言，可以减少部分重复性的分析整理工作，把更多时间投入课堂讲评和个别指导；对于教研而言，则可以基于真实教学数据更加系统地发现共性问题和教学重点。 图注：SoulAgent教师AI分身结合教师专业标准，为作文批改、课堂讲评和后续教学提供辅助。 走进校园现场，与一线师生面对面交流两次活动期间，不同学科教师结合课堂记录、备课、作业反馈、教学答疑等实际任务了解和体验SoulAgent，学生也围绕知识问答、课后学习和持续追问等场景进行互动。通过问卷、共创墙和面对面交流，师生分享了对AI辅助教学与学习的实际感受和期待。从帮助教师提升教学效率，到为学生提供更具体的反馈和持续追问支持，AI的价值正在从“更快完成任务”进一步走向“更好支持思考”：让教师把更多专业时间投入教学设计与学生指导，也让学生把更多注意力投入理解、判断和深入思考。  图注：师生围绕SoulAgent教育应用进行现场体验与交流。 未来，智源研究院将继续与中国人民大学附属中学在教育领域深化合作，围绕真实课堂、教研和学习场景持续探索AI教育应用。同时，SoulAgent也将进一步拓展教育、会议智能服务、专家分身等更多应用方向，让“越用越

articles.title: Honeycomb-Surfels: Compact Hexagonal Primitives for Efficient Scene Rendering and Reconstruction
articles.content: Novel view synthesis and 3D reconstruction have advanced rapidly with radiance fields and splatting, yet their memory and computational demands limit their use in resource-constrained settings. We introduce Hexels: novel planar hexagonal surface elements with a first-order spatial color field for efficient 3D scene and 2D image representation. Hexels exploit locally planar regions with smoothly varying appearance using fewer, larger primitives. Their hexagonal support provides an area- and boundary-efficient domain, while the local color field captures appearance variation within each primitive. Across 34 scenes, Hexels improve PSNR over memory-matched 2DGS by 4.53-7.38 dB across datasets while requiring lower training VRAM. We further ablate Hexels by showing that per primitive, Hexels outperform 2DGS by upto 4.74 dB while using lower training VRAM and having 2.31 times faster FPS. Even in unconstrained settings, Hexels offers complementary quality-memory trade-offs. For efficient 3D surface reconstruction, Hexels reduce error by 28.9% compared with memory-matched 2DGS across 15 DTU scans. On 6 Tanks and Temples surface scenes, Hexels achieves the highest mean F1 among compared methods (34.38%, versus 31.72% for 2DGS). We further also show that Hexels, as a general primitive, improves 2D image representation over Image-GS. Hexels push the Pareto frontier on the quality-efficiency trade-off of surface-aligned primitives.

articles.title: ThinkWorld: World Imagination Reinforces Chain-of-Dynamics Reasoning
articles.content: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have made substantial progress in robotic manipulation, but their generalization remains constrained by the diversity and coverage of action-labeled robot demonstrations. Human videos provide much broader behavioral and environmental experience, while learning from them faces a fundamental trade-off between scalable data and explicit action grounding. We introduce ThinkWorld, a VLA learning framework that grounds action reasoning in world dynamics and strengthens it through reinforcement learning with world imagination. ThinkWorld represents each action thought as a Chain-of-Dynamics (CoD), a sequence of discrete motion tokens that captures the intermediate dynamics connecting the current world to a future state and serves as a common action representation across embodiments. We first initialize CoD with action-labeled demonstrations, then predict the future induced by each CoD and reinforce those whose predictions better match the observed outcome. This enables videos without action annotations to provide direct supervision from observed state transitions, allowing human and robot experience to refine the same reasoning space. Experiments in simulation and on real robots demonstrate effective human-to-robot transfer and strong generalization to unseen tasks and environments.

articles.title: Can Discrete Tokens Serve as Semantically Lossless Representations of Visual Signals?
articles.content: Discrete visual tokens represent vision in a discrete form analogous to language, offering a native interface for multimodal modeling under a shared next-token prediction objective. However, quantization error is widely assumed to cause unavoidable semantic loss, fundamentally limiting the semantic fidelity of discrete visual tokens and positioning continuous visual representations as an intrinsic upper bound. Using multimodal understanding as a proxy for semantic fidelity, we revisit this assumption and find quantization error unreliable, as discrete representations with substantially larger errors can achieve better understanding. Instead, the effective bit budget of discrete indices emerges as a key determinant of downstream performance. However, existing quantizers eventually saturate as additional codebooks contribute progressively less semantic information. As one approach to alleviating this saturation, we introduce Factorized Vector Quantization, which quantizes complementary, fixed-dimensional views of the visual feature with symmetric parallel codebooks. It continues to improve at larger bit budgets, ultimately matching continuous visual representations in multimodal understanding. Trained on industrial-scale multimodal data, our model achieves state-of-the-art performance among discrete-representation models, outperforming UniAR and Emu3-Chat by 22.8% and 59.2%, respectively, on a nine-metric average. To our knowledge, it is also the first discrete-representation model competitive with strong continuous-representation models such as Qwen3-VL, including on fine-grained OCR tasks. We further identify the key principles and a practical recipe enabling this competitiveness. These results and insights support the potential of discrete visual representations to underpin large-scale native multimodal foundation models. Code and models are available at https://github.com/hustvl/FVQ

articles.title: When Should We Intervene at Test Time?
articles.content: Test-time adaptation helps a deployed model respond to changing inputs, but the same intervention can rescue one batch and damage the next. Updating normalization statistics, for example, can improve corrupted images yet fail when a batch contains mostly one class. Average accuracy hides these failures and cannot tell a model when to use an intervention. Target labels can guide this decision, but they are scarce and some choices are already clear. We introduce PORTAL, a controller that chooses when to deploy an intervention, which inputs to label, and when to stop querying. Each available prediction rule is a candidate, and its predictions are fixed before current feedback arrives. Every acquired label therefore evaluates all candidates on the same input. PORTAL combines these shared comparisons and directs queries toward candidates that can still overtake the current leader. It stops when the remaining labels cannot change the choice or when the possible accuracy gain no longer justifies another query. Our analysis links the required feedback to accuracy gaps and shared mistakes, explaining why some choices need much less evidence. Experiments show that this control turns an intervention that loses accuracy overall into a useful choice on selected batches. It prevents severe failures caused by changes in arrival order and preserves gains across complete corruption streams. When a fixed rule already works well, PORTAL uses little feedback to retain its performance. Periodic label checks reveal when past evidence needs refreshing and help the controller recover as conditions change. The acquired labels also train stronger candidates for future batches, and selection brings nearly all of their accuracy gains into deployment. The same feedback therefore improves both the choice made now and the predictions available to later batches.

articles.title: Heads of Security: Learned Attention Gates Improve Prompt Injection Robustness
articles.content: We introduce Heads of Security (HoS), a prompt injection defense that enforces instruction-data separation via a small set of learned per-head attention gates. HoS learns how each head should redistribute attention between trusted and untrusted tokens, enabling models to reason over untrusted content without following injected instructions. We evaluate HoS on Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct and GPT-OSS-20B. We compare it against SecAlign++, a state-of-the-art finetuning-based defense, and ASIDE, a defense that, like ours, builds instruction-data separation into the model architecture. We show that HoS offers greater robustness to adaptive attacks, better performance on standard utility benchmarks, and matches top performance on standard agentic prompt injection benchmarks. More specifically, the black-box RL-Hammer attack reaches 97% ASR against GPT-OSS-20B and 85% against SecAlign, but only 10% against HoS. Claudini, a state-of-the-art white-box attack, strengthened against HoS through autoresearch, requires 3 times more FLOPs to reach the same ASR on HoS as it does on GPT-OSS-20B or SecAlign. HoS preserves base-model utility across standard multiple-choice benchmarks and prompting setups, whereas SecAlign and ASIDE degrade in few-shot settings. On agentic benchmarks with static attacks, HoS and SecAlign perform similarly and substantially improve the security-utility trade-off over the base model. ASIDE struggles with tool use, achieving only 10% utility. These results show that prompt injection robustness can be achieved and improved through targeted attention interventions.

articles.title: Attention as Lattice Gauge Theory: Relations Interact Only Through Wilson Loops
articles.content: Relations compose through the entity they share - Alice is Bob's mother and Bob is Carol's father, so Alice is Carol's grandmother - and the order matters, since a father's mother is not a mother's father; verifying a composed relation means closing the loop. We show that if each entity's coordinate frame may be rotated independently (per-entity frame freedom), three things follow. In the pure-gauge sector, relations that share no cycle cannot interact at all. The only gauge-invariant score of a triangle is a class function of its holonomy $H = T_{ij} T_{jk} T_{ki}$ - a Wilson loop. And the only equivariant update of an edge is $U = Ψ(H)\, T_{ij}$ with $Ψ$ conjugation-equivariant. Edge attention by Wilson loops is therefore not one design among many but the unique form the symmetry permits. Three communities hold pieces of this form: the commuting-operator embeddings of knowledge graphs are its abelian (commuting) sector; AlphaFold's triangle update and the Edge Transformer have its shape - an edge updated through the third vertex - without its constraints; and lattice QCD builds it equivariantly on lattices. We instantiate the equivariant sub-family on general relational graphs as holonomy attention. With no training and composition alone, it infers unobserved $S_4$ relations on sparse graphs at 0.88 with a fifth of the edges corrupted, at or slightly below specialist synchronization algorithms, where every commutative architecture is capped at 0.083; its holonomy score flags corrupted triangles at AUC 0.99 where commuting scores are capped at 0.76 by a second selection rule, and it separates clusters without labels.

articles.title: KPPax: preprocess differentiable kinetic ODE for machine learning in atmospheric chemistry
articles.content: Atmospheric chemical mechanisms are commonly distributed in the language of the Kinetic PreProcessor (KPP), which generates efficient Fortran or C code but does not fit into the differentiable programming frameworks in which machine-learning models are developed. We present KPPax, a kinetic preprocessor that generates differentiable, just-in-time compiled, and vectorisable chemistry code in JAX from mechanisms written in the KPP language. KPPax evaluates the rate law with sparse operations in log space, which keeps it differentiable, and integrates the stiff system with the implicit solvers and the forward- and reverse-mode adjoints of the \texttt{diffrax} library, so that exact sensitivities are obtained without hand-derived adjoint code. We demonstrate two applications with the POLLU benchmark mechanism. In the first, the Fisher information matrix computed from an automatically differentiated Jacobian predicts, before any fit, which of the 25 rate coefficients a flow-tube-like design can identify, and noisy synthetic estimation confirms the predicted uncertainties of the nine identifiable rate coefficients to within about 30\% while revealing clusters of fast reactions of which only ratios are constrained. In the second, a neural-network correction of an emission inventory is trained offline on per-scenario 4D-Var retrievals and then fine-tuned online through the chemical model, which reduces the error of the biogenic correction by a factor of 2.4--5 and recovers information on low-temperature emissions that the individual retrievals lose. KPPax makes KPP mechanisms directly usable for parameter estimation and hybrid physics--machine-learning modelling.

articles.title: Pushing Dexterity and Safety for In-Hand Object Pose Reaching That Works Remarkably Well
articles.content: Dexterous manipulation with multi-fingered hands is the next frontier of robotics, yet learned hand skills remain limited to simple grasps or basic repeated motions, such as rotating an object. As robots attempt more demanding in-hand maneuvers, safety, such as not dropping the object, becomes critical, yet it is rarely measured. We study in-hand object pose reaching, a task that demands diverse and difficult grasps: moving an object to almost any position and orientation within reach of the fingers, at any wrist orientation, through long sequences of consecutive goals. We present a recipe for training such policies for a LEAP hand in simulation without human data, built on a range of insights, from diverse resets and goals via generated grasp datasets to an adaptive friction curriculum. With careful system identification, the policies transfer zero-shot to the real hand, using either motion capture or a single wrist-mounted depth camera, and prove remarkably capable and robust. On top of the task policy, we add a learned residual safety filter with adjustable conservativeness, letting us tune the balance between performance and safety and greatly reduce object drops. In 13.3 hours of real-robot evaluation over 4,800 unseen goals across 4 objects and diverse wrist orientations, the state-based policy reaches 95.2% of goals within 2 cm and 0.4 rad, and the filter cuts its drops by 75% while still reaching 91.5% of goals. The policies can also spin a lightbulb held in an arbitrary pose, reach out-of-distribution goals, withstand fast arm motion and perturbations, and, needing only a wrist camera, serve as portable skills such as screwing in a lightbulb. We release the full recipe as a platform for studying performance, reliability, and safety in high-dimensional dexterous systems. Videos and more are available at https://ian-chuang.github.io/dexsafe/.

articles.title: GEPA-Curator: Curated Learning for Self Improving Agents
articles.content: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used in multi-turn agentic workloads that require sustained interaction with complex environments. Existing reflective prompt optimizers such as GEPA learn from failed rollouts, but agentic failures can also come from prompt weaknesses, harness limitations, stochastic execution, or noisy judges. We argue that such failures may not provide useful learning signal, and may even be harmful; and thus it is essential to curate which tasks are provided to the prompt optimizer for better performance. We introduce GEPA-Curator, a framework that augments the prompt optimizer to select which agent experiences should shape prompt optimization. In particular, GEPA-Curator consists of two components: task curation, which filters out tasks that are likely to provide noisy or unreliable learning signals, and prior success retrieval, which selectively retrieves past successful trajectories for a task and provides them as additional context to the prompt optimizer. We evaluate GEPA-Curator on GoBrowse, ALFWorld, AppWorld, and $τ$-bench, using both Gemini 3.1 Pro and Claude Opus 5 as optimizer models. GEPA-Curator matches or exceeds the mean performance of both baselines, with gains of up to 20.7% over GEPA and 21.2% over ACE.
