articles.title: Can LLMs Uncover Hidden Physical Laws through Free Exploration?
articles.content: Scientific discovery often begins with an unexpected observation that prompts a new research question. In a world with altered physical laws, can large language models (LLMs) notice unexpected behavior, such as heavier objects falling more slowly, and discover the law through experiments without being told what to investigate? To evaluate this ability, we introduce LongChang, an automated framework that creates simulated worlds with altered physics, where one or more laws differ from ordinary physics. The evaluated LLMs act as explorers, manipulating objects and building tools to investigate their own questions without research tasks or hints about these laws. Separate LLM agents generate and review scenes, review tool designs, and evaluate reports for correctness and experimental support using the altered physical laws and exploration records. These records guide scene evolution for further exploration, allowing the full cycle to run without human intervention. Among 12 LLMs, GPT-6-Astra achieves a discovery rate of 16.7%, while the other 11 score 0%. The exploration records reveal uninvestigated anomalies and only partial identification of the altered physical laws.

articles.title: Scaling Laws for Tool-Use Agents via Controllable Environment Synthesis
articles.content: We explore how to build performant large language model (LLM) tool-use agents that complete complex, multi-step tasks. Specifically, we study how data composition in synthetically generated tool-use environments affects the training of such agents. To do so, we propose the SynthAPI pipeline, which explicitly controls the diversity of generated environments along the axes of tools, tasks, and the databases on which the tools operate. By systematically varying SynthAPI's generation controls in 458,752 tasks across 849 trained models of four different sizes, we derive a scaling law that predicts downstream tool-use agent generalization based on the scale and composition of the synthesized environments. These predictable relationships reveal several lessons for scaling tool-use agent data. As data budgets grow, scaling tool and database diversity becomes more effective than increasing the number of tasks, and increasing data complexity yields larger gains. Scaling according to these findings yields agents that outperform models trained on data from prior work in large-scale tool-use agent and synthetic environment generation across four evaluation benchmarks.

articles.title: MuonGS: Pretraining LLMs with Relaxed Weight-Norm Control
articles.content: Weight decay and explicit weight-norm constraints improve optimizer performance in language model pretraining, yet a unified understanding of why such control helps and how much is needed remains incomplete. We analyze norm control in Muon over the entire training trajectory using the \emph{accumulated effective learning rate}, $C_T=\sum_{t<T}η_t/\|W_t\|_F$, where $η_t$ is the nominal learning rate and $η_t/\|W_t\|_F$ is the effective learning rate relative to the weight norm. For bounded update directions, accumulation over any training interval bounds relative weight displacement. We show that vanilla Muon can accumulate only logarithmically, potentially limiting exploration and helping explain its slower empirical progress, whereas MuonW and MuonH guarantee at least linear accumulation under the stated conditions. Going beyond bounded-norm control, we show that sufficiently slow norm growth guarantees faster accumulation than the logarithmic worst case, opening up less restrictive optimizer designs.   Based on this insight, we propose MuonGS, which uses Gram--Schmidt (GS) projection to remove the radial component of each Muon update without fixing the weight norm. With bounded update directions and a constant nominal learning rate, we prove that the weight norm grows at most proportionally to $\sqrt{t}$ after $t$ steps. Consequently, MuonGS guarantees $C_T=Ω(\sqrt{T})$, with accumulation sustained even in later training. Further, for smooth scale-invariant objectives we establish its $O(T^{-1/2})$ stationarity guarantee. In pretraining experiments with 160M- and 400M-parameter dense models as well as a 135M active- and 1B total- parameter MoE model, MuonGS achieves lower validation perplexity than MuonH at long training horizons. In particular, for the dense model it achieves an estimated token-equivalent speedup up to about $15\%$ at matched validation loss to MuonH.

articles.title: Multi-State Linear Attention with Generalized Second-Order Routing
articles.content: Self-attention plays a key role in long-sequence modeling, but its quadratic time complexity fundamentally limits the scaling of Large Language Models. Recently, Multi-State Linear Attention (MSLA) mechanisms have been proposed to make sequence modeling more efficient by splitting the context into segments and compressing each in its own memory state. MSLA aggregates the information extracted from each memory state using only the mean alignment between a query and each segment's keys, ignoring how the alignment is distributed within the segment. In order to model the relevance of a segment to a query more comprehensively and incorporate the variance of the alignment in the aggregation, we propose MERLIN (MomEnt Routing for multi-state LINear attention), a method that tracks the first and second moments of each segment's keys. Using the moments of keys, a query can recover both the mean and the variance of its alignment with each segment to perform a more content-aware aggregation of per-state readouts. Experiments on multi-state variants of Gated DeltaNet-1.3B and Mamba-2-780M show that MERLIN consistently outperforms existing aggregation methods on various long-context tasks. In particular, MERLIN outperforms baselines on RULER needle-in-a-haystack and long-context QA (+8.3% for Gated DeltaNet-1.3B and +7.0% for Mamba-2-780M) and diverse subtasks in LongBench (+13.5% and +12.0%). It even outperforms baselines that consume 4x more memory. MERLIN provides a simple and general routing mechanism for improving long-context capabilities of MSLA models.

articles.title: Metacognitive Decoding: Efficient Inference for Diffusion Language Agents
articles.content: Diffusion language models offer a promising path to efficient agents through parallel token generation. However, efficient interaction requires adapting both where computation is spent and how much text is generated. We introduce a metacognitive controller that guides diffusion generation according to the needs of the current response and the agent's interaction with the environment. It learns when to finalize tokens and how far generation should extend, reducing overall computation within responses. Our controller, a lightweight plug-in for the diffusion backbone, is trained on agent trajectories to balance correctness and generation cost. This approach connects the agent's generation process to the interaction the agent serves. Experiments across five benchmarks demonstrate that our approach reduces inference FLOPs by 20.6% on average compared with the most efficient baseline, while maintaining competitive task accuracy. Ablation studies further validate the effectiveness of our approach.

articles.title: Repurposing Video Diffusion Transformers for Cross-View Temporal Object Correspondence
articles.content: Cross-view object correspondence identifies the same object across views. However, existing methods often rely on frame-wise matching or sequential tracking, which can propagate correspondence errors under appearance changes or occlusions. Therefore, we introduce cross-view temporal object correspondence, which requires preserving object identity across both views and time from a query mask. To address this, we propose XTrack, a unified framework which repurposes a pretrained video DiT with semantic and spatiotemporal priors for RGB-to-mask latent transport, jointly modeling cross-view matching and temporal tracking. However, naive video DiTs do not guarantee accurate cross-view grounding and often attend to semantically similar yet incorrect objects across views. Thus, we introduce focal cross-view attention alignment, hard negative conditioning, and local context crop strategies to ensure reliable grounding. Finally, beyond these architectural enhancements, we also tackle the lack of dense annotation by introducing a pseudo-label curation pipeline that converts sparse Ego-Exo4D annotations into dense supervision to enable effective video-level training. Our results demonstrate the effectiveness of XTrack as a unified framework, ensuring robust temporal consistency and identity preservation.

articles.title: What Improves During Pretraining? Tracking Knowledge Acquisition with Point-in-Time Models
articles.content: Language models pretrained on web corpora collected over multiple years learn both general and domain-specific knowledge. How these different kinds of knowledge are learned as pretraining progresses remains unclear. Recent point-in-time models trained on web snapshots from different years provide a way to probe how knowledge prevalence varies over time. Using these models, we propose a temporal variability score (TVS), defined as the coefficient of variation of an item's negative log-likelihood across models. A higher score suggests that the knowledge may be less consistently represented across years of web text. We evaluate six benchmarks covering diverse topics using six models from multiple open-source model families. We find that low- and high-TVS items are learned similarly early in training, but high-TVS items improve faster later on. At the end of the pretraining run, high-TVS items outperform low-TVS items in 34 of 36 model-benchmark settings, with an average advantage of 7.3 points of chance-normalized accuracy. This pattern is most robust on knowledge-intensive tasks, even when comparing items of similar difficulty. Our findings reveal differences in how knowledge is learned over the course of pretraining, with temporal variability providing a diagnostic of these learning dynamics beyond aggregate benchmark scores.

articles.title: Know, then Draw: A New Learning Paradigm for Visual Generation
articles.content: Visual generation requires both high-level semantic knowledge and fine-grained pixel details. We propose a learning paradigm that assigns these roles to autoregressive pretraining for knowledge acquisition and diffusion post-training for high-fidelity rendering. Within this framework, we study the objective, representation, and scaling of knowledge acquisition and rendering. Controlled comparisons identify autoregression as the stronger pretraining objective for downstream rendering, improving both learning efficiency and final generation quality. We further find that AR-only generation quality does not necessarily correlate with final performance; semantic quality matters more. This motivates a purely semantic tokenizer trained with language supervision alone, without an image decoder or reconstruction loss. We establish compute-optimal scaling laws for knowledge acquisition and rendering, and find that autoregressive pretraining lowers the fitted asymptotic rendering loss compared with pixel diffusion models trained from scratch. Guided by the laws, we train a 3B-parameter text-to-image model with only 6,600 H100 GPU-hours, achieving 86 on GenEval and 87 on DPG-Bench and validating the proposed paradigm at scale.

articles.title: Rare, Relevant, and Still Wrong: How Memory Fails LLM Group Decisions
articles.content: When an LLM group's discussion is compressed into a short memory for a final decision maker, what should the memory keep? Two natural heuristics keep the rarest claims or the claims relevant to the decision criteria. On hidden-profile tasks both look attractive, because how widely a fact is held is confounded with whether it helps. We introduce CrossProfile, a diagnostic benchmark of 60 templates with automatically verified answer keys, in which the ownership of supporting, decoy, and irrelevant facts is crossed while their text is held fixed (480 tasks). Across Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.1-8B, and two DeepSeek models, both heuristics fail in predictable places. Selecting by relevance readmits decoys, because decoys are on topic: even a perfect relevance filter loses 23 to 31 points to rarest-first selection in the classic hidden-profile configuration. Rarest-first selection is no better than random selection on average and wins only where the rare facts happen to be the useful ones. In both cases accuracy follows the balance of evidence the memory keeps, not the policy that kept it. The decision model adds a third failure, a form of social proof: it gives extra weight to facts attributed to many agents. Removing the attribution tags, or reassigning them at random with line order fixed, raises accuracy in the classic configuration by 13 to 24 points. In natural discussions the evidence is lost before any memory acts: the complete transcript yields lower accuracy than no notes at all.

articles.title: Perceiving and Predicting Dynamic Sports: Spatiotemporal Intelligence in Vision Models for Egocentric Tennis Video
articles.content: Agile robots require spatiotemporal intelligence to interpret scenes, reason about interactions, and anticipate future events. Yet it remains unclear how well foundation vision models support these capabilities, particularly from a moving egocentric camera, which is a natural view for robots. To investigate this, we collect an annotated tennis dataset and train a suite of vision models on spatiotemporal tasks. Our dataset contains egocentric video synchronized with five allocentric videos, estimated global positions, labeled contact times, and annotated stroke types. We then evaluate seven prediction tasks from egocentric images: 2D ego player and 3D ball localization, future player and ball trajectories, forehand or backhand stroke anticipation, time to the next ego player ball contact, and 3D ball position at that contact. We compare image encoders, video encoders, and vision-language models with jointly trained prediction heads. The best performing models achieve mean current-frame localization errors of 0.14 m for the ego player and 0.54 m for the ball, future forecasting errors of 0.34 m for the ego player and 0.91 m for the ball over 1.1 s, and a mean contact-time prediction error of 0.14 s. Auxiliary depth information substantially improves 3D ball localization, suggesting that inferring metric depth remains a challenge. Longer image histories do not improve ball forecasting, indicating that representations exploit scene context rather than rely solely on inter-frame motion. Finally, we propose a conditional diffusion model to generate whole-body kinematic tennis motion from vision encoder predictions on egocentric video at real-time rates, adapting movements as predictions are refined. These results move towards a deeper understanding of how foundation vision models can support real-time dynamic robots using egocentric video.

articles.title: VideoLVR: Latent Visual Reasoning over Grounded Video Evidence
articles.content: Chain-of-thought reasoning has substantially advanced video understanding in multimodal large language models (MLLMs). However, language-based reasoning traces do not provide a reliable mechanism for models to revisit relevant visual evidence, leading to visual forgetting and impairing their ability to reason over video content. Existing approaches maintain visual grounding during reasoning in two main ways: they either refer to evidence using textual coordinates, which specify symbolic locations rather than the visual content itself, or reinsert cropped regions or frames into the multimodal context, preserving visual details at the cost of substantial context expansion. To address these limitations, we introduce VideoLVR, which constructs latent visual evidence from local regions at relevant video moments, thereby providing visual support for intermediate reasoning steps. To supervise latent visual evidence generation, we introduce a visual token prediction objective that formulates visual token reconstruction as prediction over a vocabulary derived from the input video, thereby unifying visual evidence reconstruction and text generation within the same token prediction framework. This shared prediction framework enables MLLMs to reason over interleaved text tokens and latent visual states while integrating evidence from different moments. We further extend VideoLVR to reinforcement learning by treating sampled visual tokens as actions alongside text tokens and jointly optimizing the policy using final-answer rewards. By efficiently revisiting task-relevant visual information during reasoning, VideoLVR improves video understanding without substantially expanding the multimodal context. Experiments on multiple video benchmarks demonstrate its effectiveness, especially on tasks requiring fine-grained visual evidence.

articles.title: EnvSched: Environment-Aware Scheduling for Rollout-Efficient Agent Reinforcement Learning
articles.content: As executable environments for language agents scale, generating and verifying their rollouts becomes increasingly expensive. Under finite rollout budgets, this raises an important question: can data management at the environment level make agentic reinforcement learning (RL) more efficient by organizing, evaluating, and scheduling task instances together with the environments that determine their tools, states, transitions, and verification? To address this question, we introduce EnvSched (Environment-aware Scheduling), an online scheduler that learns from rollout history. EnvSched assigns scheduling value through two complementary modeling choices: exploitation prioritizes tasks likely to provide informative reward differences, while coverage spreads each batch across underobserved environments and interaction patterns. EnvSched organizes environment--task pairs as nodes in a dual-relation graph, with within-environment edges capturing task semantics and shared tool, state, and verifier structure, and cross-environment edges capturing abstract execution and reward topology. By propagating historical rollout statistics along both edge types, it predicts within-task reward variance. These predictions guide a scheduler that allocates each batch to tasks with high predicted reward variance and underobserved environments and tasks. Environment quotas and a similarity penalty further limit concentration and redundancy, yielding informative and diverse batches without additional pilot rollouts. In RL on Qwen3-8B, EnvSched achieves an average score of 48.81 across BFCL-v3, tau-Bench, and ACEBench-Agent after 40 training steps, exceeding the highest score attained by random task selection after 120 steps. It also improves downstream performance across model sizes at the same training budget.

articles.title: Beyond Answer Changes: Matched Same-Class Controls for Local Audio Evidence
articles.content: For audio-language models, an answer change after a local sound-event edit can reflect a response to the event's class, sensitivity to waveform rewriting, or both. We compare matched same-class and different-class replacements of a queried event. Both use the same interval, level estimate, donor fitting, and crossfade, while the same-class replacement preserves the correct answer. Across 600 synthetic soundscapes and three models from two architecture families, different-class replacements produce 49.7 to 60.9 percentage points more answer changes than same-class replacements. Same-class accuracy remains within 5.2 percentage points of original accuracy. Among trials with correct original and same-class answers, soundscape-weighted selective accuracy for the inserted class is 73.7 to 81.9%, averaging eligible trials within each soundscape and then weighting eligible soundscapes equally. This protocol tests how model answers respond to local changes in event class.

articles.title: RESPLE2: Inertial-Informed Recursive Non-Uniform Spline Estimation for Multi-Sensor Odometry with Global Refinement
articles.content: We present RESPLE2, a recursive multi-sensor state estimation framework using non-uniform B-splines for 6-DoF motion representation. By exploiting the knot-clamping boundary property, we propose a theoretically grounded mechanism for exact control-point prediction directly informed by inertial kinematics along the trajectory, with knot placement adapted to motion and measurement availability. Within an iterated extended Kalman filter, we perform this prediction using a subset of inertial measurements. A subsequent reset step preserves trajectory consistency as the knots extend. The update step further incorporates heterogeneous sensor measurements at their native timestamps through continuous-time observation models, supporting flexible combinations of LiDARs, cameras, inertial measurement units, and leg kinematics. We further develop a lightweight global optimization module that directly refines non-uniform B-spline control points by incorporating loop-closure constraints derived from LiDAR-visual cues. We conduct extensive evaluations on public and experimental datasets across handheld, tracked, legged, and hybrid aerial-legged platforms, covering highly dynamic maneuvers with extreme accelerations. Compared with state-of-the-art multi-sensor odometry systems, RESPLE2 achieves competitive or superior estimation accuracy and robustness in the corresponding sensor configurations, particularly under aggressive motion, while maintaining real-time operation. We publicly release our code and experimental datasets at https://github.com/ASIG-X/RESPLE2.

articles.title: MoI-Bench: A Benchmark for Image Generation and Editing on Mobile Devices
articles.content: Developing on-device image models requires considering practical user needs, task types and device resource constraints. However, existing benchmarks provide limited guidance on identifying capability gaps between on-device models and server-side models. We introduce MoI-Bench, a benchmark grounded in mobile user needs, comprising 64 subtasks and 1150 samples. It defines 16 operations, such as removal and replacement, and eight visual target categories covering content such as portraits and text. These form two orthogonal axes whose applicable combinations define specific tasks, such as removing facial makeup. To better guide model improvement, we further propose MoI-Eval, which introduces task-specific criteria covering instruction following, visual quality and detail preservation. We further construct sample-level evaluation questions and aggregate their scores into overall quality and capability profiles along the operation, target and criteria axes. We evaluate representative on-device and server-side models and measure mobile deployment costs. Results show that this decoupled Operation x Target design provides finer-grained guidance for improving compact models. For example, it highlights the need to prioritize specific capability gaps (e.g., text-replacement) over broad application-level goals (e.g., improving text editing). Unlike conventional benchmarks that rank models using a single score, we introduce a two-dimensional Quality-Deployability capability map to assess models for practical mobile use. The map shows that current on-device models can achieve efficient generation or editing but expanding their task coverage deserves greater attention than further improving deployment efficiency. Further progress requires improving editing quality, particularly identity preservation and text rendering, while broadening task coverage.

articles.title: GAS-PFN: Graph-Aware Spatiotemporal Prior-Data Fitted Networks for Zero-Shot Traffic Forecasting
articles.content: Traffic forecasting requires modeling complex temporal dynamics and the spatial dependencies imposed by road topology. Supervised graph-based models achieve strong performance, but are often trained for a particular dataset and sensor graph, making deployment to new or evolving networks costly. Prior-Data Fitted Networks (PFNs) offer a zero-shot alternative by learning in-context inference from synthetic task priors, which provide an explicit mechanism for encoding domain-specific assumptions. Existing forecasting PFNs, however, do not explicitly represent the graph-structured dependencies governing traffic dynamics. To combine graph-aware traffic modeling with zero-shot adaptation, we introduce the Graph-Aware Spatiotemporal Prior-Data Fitted Network (GAS-PFN). GAS-PFN incorporates sampled road topology into its synthetic task prior through random-walk diffusion, teaching the model to learn graph-coupled dynamics during pretraining. Its co-designed inference architecture uses two mask-conditioned passes through a shared Transformer backbone to separately model sensor-specific temporal dynamics and spatiotemporal interactions among neighboring sensors before integrating their representations for prediction. This design enables GAS-PFN to use target-network structure and context without parameter updates. Across six benchmarks at the 90-minute horizon, GAS-PFN reduces MSE by 34.0% on average relative to TimePFN, its closest PFN-based predecessor. It also reduces MSE by 27.7% on average relative to four recent industry-developed general-purpose zero-shot forecasters. In this comparison, all models receive 90 minutes of contiguous recent history, and any additional context is drawn from each dataset's chronological training split. These results indicate that aligning PFN priors and inference architectures with graph structure improves in-context learning for zero-shot traffic forecasting.

articles.title: Understanding the limits of latent world models
articles.content: World models are widely proposed as core components for enabling agents to reason over long temporal and spatial horizons. Yet current evaluations often emphasize task performance while providing limited insight into whether learned world models acquire predictive latent dynamics that reflect the underlying structure of the environment. Here we introduce the concept of faithful latent world models as an equivariance condition between the environment's transition map and the learned latent dynamics. We propose latent rollout consistency (LRC) as a metric to evaluate action-conditioned latent prediction. Strikingly, we find that across the studied state of the art latent world models, none solves the task by actually faithfully modeling the dynamics of the environment.

articles.title: Timestral
articles.content: We introduce Timestral, a family of four time series foundation models for probabilistic forecasting, with 5M, 28M, 123M, and 209M parameters. Timestral sets a new state of the art on GIFT-Eval, TIME, and fev-bench, where Timestral-209M and Timestral-123M take the top two places on every metric. We achieve this with three ingredients: Decoupled Horizon Forecasting (DHF), which separates prediction tokens from the causally encoded context, so that longer horizons are trained without masking context and each observed value is both a forecast target and context for later forecasts; a covariate framework that natively supports known-future covariates within a causal architecture; and a two-stage pipeline that pretrains exclusively on a diverse, large-scale synthetic corpus before post-training on a mix of real and synthetic data with extended context. This report describes the model design and its benchmark results. Weights for all four models are available on Hugging Face and inference code on GitHub.

articles.title: REGER: Modeling inter-item Relations with Semantic IDs for Generative Recommendation
articles.content: Personalized recommendation depends on learning semantic and collaborative relations among items from online content and user interactions. Generative recommendation (GR) offers a promising paradigm by autoregressively generating discrete semantic IDs (SIDs) of items. However, randomly initialized SID token embeddings and GR models trained from scratch do not directly inherit the semantic relations inherent in items, while inter-item collaborative relations are learned largely implicitly through token-level attention and next-token supervision. To address this limitation, we propose REGER, a unified framework that explicitly incorporates inter-item relations into semantic pretraining, history encoding, and SID generation. We pretrain the GR model through generative semantic retrieval, enabling it to inherit inter-item semantic similarity by learning to generate semantic neighbors' SIDs. We combine global attention with local attention aligned with SID boundaries to capture historical context and directed transitions between adjacent items. We further develop a theoretical framework for hierarchical preference decomposition over the SID prefix tree, proving an exact factorization of collaborative preference distributions and a weighted decomposition of item-level KL divergence into prefix-conditional KL divergences. Building on this analysis, we distill a discriminative teacher's full conditional distributions over all legal next tokens at ground-truth prefixes along the target SID path, jointly optimizing this objective with cross-entropy. Extensive experiments on real-world datasets demonstrate consistent improvements over existing GR baselines and support the effectiveness of the proposed preference distillation.

articles.title: Zero-Shot Multimodal Event Spotting in Soccer Broadcasts
articles.content: Automatic soccer event spotting supports highlight generation, video indexing, and sports analytics, but existing methods depend on large annotated datasets and soccer-specific training. We present a zero-shot framework that detects, classifies, and temporally localizes events in full-length soccer broadcasts without task-specific parameter training. Each match is segmented into overlapping clips represented by a compact visual storyboard and the aligned commentary transcript, which a general-purpose multimodal model processes jointly. On three manually annotated matches containing 130 events, the best configuration achieves 72.0% F1@5s and outperforms SoccerNet-trained CALF and NetVLAD++ in a cross-dataset setting, while the storyboard representation reduces inference cost by 72% compared with individual frames. We further analyze the effects of model family, input representation, and prompt optimization, and introduce an evidence-grounded excitement-scoring stage that ranks detected events with natural-language explanations for highlight selection.

articles.title: EgoThumb: A Vision-Driven Supernumerary Robotic Thumb for Autonomous Grasp and Holding Assistance
articles.content: Supernumerary robotic fingers augment human dexterity by enabling a single hand to perform complex "hold-and-manipulate" tasks that typically require bimanual coordination. However, existing devices are often hindered by bulky hardware that limits interaction to large objects and rely on explicit hand motion triggers that lack environmental context. To address these challenges, we present EgoThumb, a fully open-source, vision-driven supernumerary robotic thumb. EgoThumb features a compact, dual tendon-driven finger whose actuation is relocated to the forearm, reducing distal weight while enabling precise active joint control. The system utilizes a visual imitation learning policy that maps egocentric images from a palm-facing camera directly to continuous joint positions. By implicitly decoding human intent from visual cues capturing both the hand and the object of interest, EgoThumb achieves robust autonomous manipulation and strong generalization across diverse users and environments. All hardware designs and software implementations are fully open-sourced at https://ego-thumb.github.io.

articles.title: GLM-5.5 要来了？唐杰最新论文，曝出智谱神秘模型
articles.content: 图像生成正确率 54%，文字问答仅 14.57%。    作者丨郑佳美    编辑丨岑   峰                                                                                                       智谱内部的 GLM-Omni，先在一篇论文里露了面。这篇研究由清华大学与智谱 AI 联合完成，唐杰担任通讯作者。模型名称刚刚出现在论文中，社交平台上就有人把它与 GLM-5.5 联系起来。虽然论文并没有披露版本对应关系，但给出了 GLM-Omni 的技术底座，以及它在统一视觉理解和图像生成方面的一组实验结果。参考链接：https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.21459其中一组数据尤其扎眼：经过图像生成训练，GLM-Omni 在数字任务中，把指定号码正确画在球衣上的比例达到 72%，研究人员拿走图片，改用文字询问球衣号码，正确率却只有 2%。模型已经能在画面里复现的知识，换成一句问话，竟然几乎答不上来。这恰好戳中了统一多模态模型的一处技术瓶颈。过去，图像理解负责看，图像生成负责画。如今两种能力逐渐进入同一套架构，模型在学习生成物体、地图和文字图案时，也会接触大量未被语言描述的视觉信息。可图像里学来的东西，究竟能有多少被语言推理使用，光看生成效果很难知道。而智谱的这篇文章正是试着沿着知识进入模型、再被调用的过程，把这个问题拆开来看。01KTP：把答案留在图片里要确认生成训练有没有教给模型新知识，先得绕开它已有的记忆。让模型生成现实球队的球衣，即使号码画对了，也可能只是因为它早在文字资料中读到过。雷峰网研究人员因此搭建了一个虚构世界 MagicWorld，给从未存在过的实体安排颜色、号码和空间关系，让目标知识尽量只从此次训练的图片里进入模型。例如，一件虚构球衣叫 Arvenbrock，号码设为 10。训练时，文字提示只要求生成这件球衣，数字 10 只出现在目标图像中。等模型完成训练，研究人员再直接问它 Arvenbrock 的球衣号码。如果能回答 10，就有理由认为它把图像里的实体属性关联带进了文字回答。这套数据并不只有球衣。团队设计了颜色、数量、形状、空间排列、相对大小、数字和文字 7 类任务，每类 50 条知识，共 350 条，再为每个实体制作不同背景和视角的图像，筛选后留下 8552 组训练样本。训练文本还经过检查，尽量排除答案泄漏和属性分布不均造成的干扰。不同任务也能拉开知识类型的差别：形状与颜色往往属于有限类别，空间排列要求理解对象之间的位置关系，球衣号码和书籍标题则需要记住具体的字符序列有了这批受控知识，研究人员分别测试两条路径：一条让模型重新生成目标图片，再检查图中的属性，另一条不提供图片，只用文字提问。前者衡量模型能否在生成过程中复现关联，后者衡量它能否直接把关联转成语言答案。这样就能区分模型根本没学会某项属性，还是已经会画，却无法从文字端调用。参与实验的三种模型采用不同架构。BAGEL 将理解和生成放在相对独立的专家分支中，SenseNova-U1 直接建模图像像素，GLM-Omni 则从 GLM-4.1V-Thinking 的预训练模型出发，接入基于 X-Omni 的离散图像 Tokenizer。研究还加入 10000 条与目标知识无关的文字问答，让模型熟悉回答形式，却不提前得到答案。02会画却不会说，问题卡在哪里直接测试出来的差距，比球衣案例更普遍。BAGEL 的平均视觉正确率为 31.43%，文字回答只有 8.86%，GLM-Omni 分别为 54.00% 和 14.57%，SenseNova-U1 则为 61.14% 和 20.00%。SenseNova-U1 在号码任务中的视觉正确率甚至达到 88%，纯文字回答却是 0%。图像生成的训练目标，是让模型根据名称和提示重建视觉内容。只要实体与属性的关联能帮助还原图片，就可以通过训练得到强化，但文字问答还要沿着语言输出路径找到对应属性，并把它变成字符或词语。共享参数不意味着这些路径已经互相打通。

articles.title: 源创计划首期路演：五个AI硬科技项目集中亮相，智源学者加速从实验室走向产业一线
articles.content: 从底层芯片、神经形态计算，到机器人自主部署、极端环境物理智能和地表物理环境建模，人工智能前沿技术正沿着多条不同路径推进产业应用落地。如何让实验室里的原创成果跨越工程验证与商业化之间的距离，成为科研创新走向产业实践的重要课题。10月26日，北京智源人工智能研究院发布的“源创计划”首期路演在中关村国际技术交易中心举办。临界核科技、灵枢启智、张量场科技、苍穹极智、潜向量科技五个项目集中亮相，分别聚焦3D自选通V-RRAM芯片、神经形态具身智能、哈密顿世界模型、极端环境的可靠物理智能、地表物理环境统一世界模型等方向。活动还设置了项目与基金洽谈环节，推动创业团队与投资机构交流对接。 从“源头创新”到“产业验证”，源创计划要打通的不只是资金活动现场，智源研究院副院长杨洋介绍了“源创计划”的定位与支持机制。作为主要面向智源学者群体的原创技术创业孵化计划，源创计划聚焦人工智能领域的原创科研课题，遵循“源头创新、快速决策、小步试行、全流程合规转化”的原则，整合技术、人才、资本与产业资源，为科研团队从实验室走向产业提供支持。计划不仅关注资金对接，更着力构建连接原创科研、创业团队与产业市场的协同机制，推动科研成果从技术发现走向工程验证与商业化应用。 源创计划的推出，也回应了人工智能产业发展与科技成果转化的现实需求。当前，AI正处于从技术突破迈向产业应用的关键阶段，原创技术的工程化验证、场景适配与商业化转化日益受到关注。与此同时，科技成果转化相关政策与机制持续完善，为科研机构探索原创成果转化提供了新的条件。源创计划希望把握这一窗口期，进一步打通科研创新与产业需求之间的连接，支持更多有潜力的原创技术走向市场。五个项目，呈现AI原创技术的多元探索1. 临界核科技：从原创器件到软硬件平台临界核科技聚焦3DV-RRAM芯片，布局底层自选通RRAM器件、芯片、FlagOS软件生态与系统应用，致力于打造软硬件协同的全栈产品体系。项目以存储级内存和存算一体为切入点，探索新型存储与AI算力协同发展的新路径，旨在突破现有计算机体系结构面临的存储与算力瓶颈。团队由清华大学国家级青年人才领衔，曾获省部级自然科学一等奖(2025年)，兼具基础研究和工程技术攻关优势。  2. 灵枢启智：以神经形态计算重构具身智能感知架构灵枢启智聚焦跨尺度多模态感知与神经形态具身智能，致力于为具身智能构建物理感知与类脑计算基础设施。项目从底层光学器件、感算一体芯片延伸至模型算法，探索从感知到决策的全栈技术架构。 其核心目标不仅是让智能体感知外部环境，还包括理解物质属性与人类意图，并在此基础上实现毫秒级自主决策。通过器件、芯片与算法的协同设计，项目探索提升具身智能环境理解与实时决策能力的新路径。 3. 张量场科技：以哈密顿世界模型推动机器人自主部署张量场科技面向人因风险高、工程师难以反复调试的高价值场景，打造由哈密顿世界模型驱动的机器人部署引擎，提供环境建模、策略生成、端侧部署与持续进化等全链条服务。 团队提出哈密顿世界模型架构，通过物理先验约束提升模型输出的物理一致性。据项目介绍，其预训练数据效率较主流方案提升3-4个数量级。模型可适配多种机器人本体，项目还提出“部署即服务”模式，计划与机器人本体厂商、硬件供应商及云计算平台协同发展。团队曾获清华大学校长杯第三名，已完成天使轮融资；公司于2026年8月在北京海淀注册成立。 4. 苍穹极智：极端环境的可靠物理智能面向深空、深地等极端环境，苍穹极智聚焦物理智能基础设施建设，试图解决极端场景下数据难以获取、模型难以训练、智能系统难以部署等问题。 团队提出AI4π（AI for Physical AI）技术范式，通过物理内嵌仿真引擎、自进化分层脑训推系统与泛本体操作系统，构建覆盖智能体设计、训练、测试与改进的技术闭环，探索突破物理智能研发中的数据与工程瓶颈。团队由国家级领军人才领衔，依托北航与智源的科研资源，已获得顶会杰出论文、世界人形机器人运动会全球季军等十余项国际奖项。目前，项目通过仿真数据订阅与系统授权探索商业化，已在园区维保、商业航天等领域获得千万元级订单。 5. 潜向量科技：以地表物理环境统一世界模型连接虚拟与现实潜向量科技聚焦地表物理环境统一世界模型，其团队自主研发EWM（Earth World Model），将大气强迫、太阳辐射等外部驱动因素，土壤、植被、水体、山地、碳循环等地表过程，以及电站、农田、工业与基础设施等人类系统纳入统一潜空间进行表征，探索构建可干预、可反演、可证伪的通用物理基座模型。 项目采用按Token计费的模型服务模式，新能源场景已在5个国家的12个站点完成实证验证。在光伏场景中，团队以自研Boson系列清洁与运
